ABOUT THE ROLE

OpenAI’s largest and most strategic customers are turning AI ambition into deployments that change how their organizations work. As a Delivery Lead, you will own delivery of priority AI initiatives for these customers, leading complex, high-impact deployments from planning through launch and adoption.



You’ll establish an integrated delivery plan, drive execution against launch commitments, resolve blockers, and lead progress toward measurable customer value. You’ll partner closely with account and technical teams, FDEs, customers, and delivery partners to turn customer priorities into successful deployments. You’ll bring a clear view of delivery progress, risks, and expected outcomes, helping teams make informed decisions and connecting successful execution to consumption and growth.



This is a senior, customer-facing role for someone who can move between executive conversations and practical details that determine whether a deployment succeeds. You bring technical fluency, sound judgment, and the ability to create clarity and drive action in complex, evolving environments.






WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own delivery of priority AI initiatives. Lead complex customer engagements from scoping and planning through deployment, launch, and initial adoption.

 - Build and drive an integrated delivery plan. Establish clear scope, milestones, accountable owners, dependencies, resource needs, and success measures across customer, OpenAI, and partner teams.

 - Resolve blockers and drive decisions. Identify risks early, work through dependencies and resource constraints, and bring the right stakeholders together to resolve tradeoffs and keep delivery moving.

 - Lead launch readiness and activation. Drive rollout and enablement planning, address technical and organizational readiness gaps, and remove barriers to initial adoption and usage.

 - Connect delivery to customer value. Define expected outcomes and measurement approaches with customers and account teams. Track adoption and consumption, assess results against agreed baselines, and communicate the value achieved.

 - Provide a clear view of delivery health. Lead customer and internal delivery reviews that drive decisions and action. Communicate progress, launch confidence, risks, and implications for expected consumption and revenue timing.

 - Improve how we deliver. Turn customer experience into repeatable playbooks, practical tools, and actionable feedback for product and delivery teams.






WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 7+ years of experience leading complex enterprise technology deployments, customer delivery programs, or transformation initiatives involving multiple teams and partners.

 - A track record of driving programs from scope through launch and adoption, with accountability for delivery commitments and measurable customer outcomes.

 - Strong technical aptitude, with the ability to understand AI systems, APIs, integrations, enterprise architecture, security dependencies, and deployment risks.

 - The ability to translate customer priorities into actionable delivery plans with clear milestones, owners, dependencies, and success measures.

 - Strong judgment under ambiguity, including the ability to identify material risks, navigate competing priorities, and drive timely decisions.

 - Experience building trust with customers and leading across teams outside your reporting line while holding stakeholders accountable to shared commitments.

 - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage executives, technical specialists, and customer operators and explain complex delivery issues clearly.

 - Commercial awareness and an understanding of how deployment, adoption, and consumption contribute to customer value and growth.

 - A practical approach to building repeatable delivery methods while adapting to the needs of individual

About the Team

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

 

About the Role

We’re looking for dedicated, experienced, and deeply curious individuals to help solve some of the most complex challenges faced by our customers while building the future of post-AGI support alongside us. In this role, you’ll work directly with customers through support tickets and live calls, troubleshooting high-impact issues and resolving novel, often ambiguous technical problems in one of the fastest-moving environments in technology. As AI adoption rapidly accelerates, the work you do will directly support mission-critical systems being built on OpenAI’s platform, serving as a critical line of defense for customers operating at massive scale.

Beyond resolving technical issues, you’ll help define what world-class support looks like in an AGI-driven future. You’ll partner closely with Engineering, Product, and Operations to improve systems, reduce bugs, and elevate the customer experience, while leveraging automation, agents, and our own AI technology to transform how support operates at scale.

Note: each person in this role will be expected to work a standard 5x8 work week, with 1 of the days covering weekend shifts each week (e.g., work weeks covering Tuesday - Saturday or Sunday - Thursday)

You’ll be responsible for:

 - Working directly with customers to troubleshoot and resolve their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, and production incidents. Providing end-to-end ownership through debugging logs, analyzing system behavior, reproducing issues, and delivering expert guidance.

 - Becoming a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and platform, serving as a go-to resource for complex technical issues.

 - Serving as a critical escalation point and line of defense for complex technical issues, partnering closely with customers and Engineering teams to troubleshoot, resolve, and proactively prevent recurring problems while leveraging scripting and emerging AI capabilities to improve internal tooling and automate operational workflows

 - Taking learnings from resolving customer issues and creating our approach to scaling these solutions, partnering with Product and Go-To-Market teams.

 - Driving operational excellence by identifying opportunities for automation and AI-powered workflows, implementing scalable improvements that increase team efficiency, reducing manual effort, and elevating the overall support experience.

 - Providing occasional holiday and weekend support on call coverage, as needed, to support business and customer needs.

 

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - Have 8+ years of experience in User Operations, Engineering, Support Engineering or similar technical roles, ideally within high-growth tech startups or other fast-paced environments.

 - Are comfortable using emerging technologies (ie. Codex, ChatGPT, OpenAI API, etc.) to script or engineer code (e.g., Python) for automating repetitive tasks and integrating tools.

 - Have expert-level SaaS troubleshooting skills with the ability to rapidly understand new technologies and complex concepts.

 - Polished enterprise communication and are calm with high-stakes customers during live incident calls

 - Proven experience building strong relationships with customers and cross-functional partners to drive resolution to complex issues.

 - Exceptional critical thinker and problem solver with the ability to clearly communicate complex technical issues to both customers and internal teams.

 - Thrive in ambiguity, adapt rapidly to change, continuously learn, and proactively seek opportunities for growth.

 - Bring a humble, team first mindset, a genuine eagerness to help others, and the curiosity to quickly learn whatever knowledge is needed to help both your teammates and our customers succeed.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, another relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

dfec3b6a297e.title: Data Engineer, Hardware & Consumer Devices
dfec3b6a297e.description:
About the team

OpenAI is building a new generation of AI-powered consumer devices, creating opportunities to bring increasingly capable AI into people's everyday lives.

Our Data Engineering team is responsible for establishing the foundational data infrastructure that supports the development, manufacturing, launch, and ongoing operation of these products. We're building the systems that connect information across the entire device lifecycle, enabling engineering, operations, and Data Science partners to understand product performance, identify problems, and make better decisions.

This is an early-stage organization with significant greenfield opportunities. We're looking for engineers who want to shape the technical foundations of a rapidly growing business and establish systems that will scale alongside our products.

About the role:

As a Data Engineer, you'll design, build, and scale the data infrastructure that powers OpenAI's hardware and consumer devices organization.

You'll tackle technically challenging problems involving complex data sources, evolving operational requirements, and systems that need to scale from early development through manufacturing and consumer deployment.

Unlike roles focused primarily on supporting individual analytics projects, this position emphasizes building durable, reusable data foundations that enable multiple teams and use cases.

You'll have significant ownership over technical decisions, work closely with partners across engineering, manufacturing, operations, and Data Science, and help define how we approach Data Engineering as the organization grows.

In this role, you will:

 - Build foundational data infrastructure: Design and implement reliable, scalable data pipelines, platforms, and datasets that support hardware development, manufacturing, customer operations, and device performance.

 - Connect complex data ecosystems: Integrate information across manufacturing systems, factory operations, device telemetry, quality assurance, and customer-facing operational systems.

 - Establish durable data models: Develop reusable datasets and data architectures that enable consistent measurement, investigation, and decision-making across multiple teams.

 - Enable manufacturing and quality intelligence: Connect manufacturing conditions and production history with downstream product performance, reliability, returns, and failure signals.

 - Prepare for scale: Design systems that evolve from early-stage development and initial production to increasingly complex operations and large-scale consumer deployment.

 - Partner across disciplines: Work with hardware and software engineers, manufacturing teams, operations leaders, and Data Scientists to translate emerging requirements into robust technical solutions.

 - Shape our technical direction: Help establish engineering standards, architectural principles, data quality practices, and infrastructure decisions that will influence the organization for years to come.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Are comfortable making architectural decisions as requirements evolve and the right solutions aren't immediately obvious.

 - Are highly self-directed and can take broad, ambiguous problems from exploration through implementation.

 - Enjoy working directly with cross-functional partners and understanding how technical decisions affect real products and operational outcomes.

 - Have a builder's mentality and are energized by creating foundational systems rather than exclusively optimizing mature infrastructure.

 - Hold a high bar for engineering quality while remaining pragmatic about the speed and flexibility required in an early-stage environment.

Minimum Qualifications:

 - Have exceptional Data Engineering fundamentals and a track record of designing, building, and operating complex data systems.

 - Bring strong technical judgment around data architecture, distributed systems, data modeling, reliability, and scalability.

 - Have experience developing production-grade pipelines and infrastructure across heterogeneous data sources.

Bonus points if you have:

 - Experience with hardware, consumer electronics, connected devices, or IoT.

 - Experience building data infrastructure for manufacturing, factory operations, or supply-chain systems.

 - Familiarity with device telemetry, reliability engineering, product quality, or failure analysis.

 - Experience supporting customer operations, technical support, or Trust & Safety.

 - A track record of building data platforms or foundational infrastructure in a startup or rapidly scaling organization.



Prior hardware experience is not required. We value exceptional engineering ability, intellectual curiosity, and the capacity to learn new domains quickly.

About the Team

OpenAI Presence, part of Enterprise Engineering, builds a platform for reliable AI agents that carry out high-volume business workflows. We focus on specific use cases such as customer support, sales, and insurance claims, helping organizations put agents to work in production.

The Presence platform supports the agent development lifecycle, including evaluation, deployment, and improvement through real interactions. It connects agents to company systems and supports voice and chat experiences, with policies, guardrails, and human handoffs to help businesses stay in control. Read the launch announcement https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/.

About the Role

We’re looking for an engineer to help shape the foundations of Presence and build the systems that make AI agents dependable in everyday business operations. You’ll help set the platform’s technical direction while staying close to the code, taking architecture from early decisions through to systems that perform reliably at scale.

You’ll bring deep backend expertise and the product judgment to connect what we build with how businesses use it. The work centers on the services that power Presence and extends across the stack—giving you scope to shape both the underlying systems and the experiences they enable.

In this role, you will:

 - Provide hands-on technical leadership, guiding architectural decisions and implementation across the Presence platform.

 - Design and build backend systems for reliable, high-volume agent workflows in support, sales, and other enterprise use cases.

 - Develop platform capabilities that support agent development and learning from real-world use.

 - Identify and address reliability bottlenecks as agent workflows become more complex and usage grows.

 - Work across backend infrastructure and product experiences as needed, collaborating with other engineers to turn evolving requirements into working software.

Your background might look something like:

 - 9+ years of professional engineering experience, excluding internships, in backend, platform, or product engineering roles.

 - A track record of hands-on technical leadership, including setting architecture, breaking complex problems into clear implementation plans, and guiding engineers through delivery.

 - Deep backend engineering and systems design skills, with proficiency in at least one backend programming language and experience designing services, data models, and interfaces that remain reliable as usage grows.

 - End-to-end ownership of complex systems or product capabilities, from ambiguous requirements and technical design through implementation, launch, and production iteration.

 - Strong production engineering judgment: you can diagnose difficult failures, reason about performance and scalability, and improve reliability through testing, observability, and operational discipline.

 - Strong product judgment that connects technical decisions to user needs, with the ability to balance delivery speed, reliability, security, and long-term maintainability.

 - The ability to move between backend infrastructure and product experiences, contribute across the stack when needed, and quickly learn unfamiliar systems, tools, and domains.

About the Team

Enterprise Controls & Console is part of Enterprise Engineering. We build the permissions, governance, and administration capabilities that help organizations use and deploy ChatGPT, Codex, and OpenAI products with confidence. We give administrators granular controls over access and security, helping ensure that people and agents operate within the boundaries their organizations define.

Our work combines complex backend platform engineering with enterprise product needs and touches every major product and model launch. We build scalable, reusable services and intuitive administration experiences, and provide a shared controls foundation that enables internal teams to introduce new capabilities safely.

We are looking for an experienced backend software engineer to help shape and build the systems behind enterprise access, governance, and sharing. dd6b6e86801f.description:
About the Team

OpenAI is on a bold mission to build the world’s most advanced AI infrastructure. We are seeking a Data Center Network and Structured Cabling Engineer with 10+ years of experience in designing and implementing optimized network and structured cabling solutions at large data centers buildings and data center campuses.

The Data Center Engineering team is central to this mission defining infrastructure strategy, driving technical innovation, working with research to set performance benchmarks, and developing reference designs that enable rapid, scalable global deployment.

As part of this team, you will help design and deliver next-generation data center infrastructure optimized for AI workloads. You’ll collaborate across research, site selection, design, construction, commissioning, hardware engineering, deployment, operations, and global partners to bring OpenAI’s infrastructure vision to life.

Role Summary

As a Physical Network & Structured Cabling Engineer, you will own the design, implementation, and quality assurance of structured cabling and physical network infrastructure across OpenAI’s global data center footprint. This role bridges design, construction, and operations, ensuring that every layer of our physical networking from fiber trunks to copper patching meets the highest standards of performance, reliability, and scalability.

Key Responsibilities

 - Design and specify physical network infrastructure across data center buildings and campuses, including fiber and copper cabling, network rooms, rack layouts, cable trays, and duct bank pathways. Coordinate with other engineering disciplines to ensure network infrastructure space, power, cooling, and operational requirements are incorporated into the overall design

 - Develop standards, reference designs, and installation guidelines for structured cabling and physical network deployments.

 - Translate logical network architectures and hardware connectivity requirements into scalable physical designs, including fiber topology, port connectivity, patching, redundancy, and capacity planning, in partnership with network engineering and operations teams.

 - Provide technical direction to design consultants, cabling vendors, and installation contractors, resolving scope gaps and ensuring designs are constructible and meet network requirements.

 - Define installation quality and acceptance criteria, and oversee inspection, testing, commissioning, and turnover of structured cabling systems.

 - Lead physical network design reviews, coordinate clash detection and resolution with other disciplines, and conduct site inspections to verify installation quality and conformance with design and operational requirements.

 - Troubleshoot and resolve issues during build, commissioning, and handover phases to ensure network readiness.

 - Develop and maintain physical network documentation, including design requirements, drawings, port maps, cable schedules, bills of materials, labeling standards, and as-built records.

 - Provide feedback to design and operations teams to drive continuous improvement of physical network standards.

Qualifications

 - Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Telecommunications, or related field, or equivalent experience.

 - 10+ years of experience designing and delivering physical network infrastructure and structured cabling systems for large-scale data centers, including responsibility for design decisions, construction coordination, and operational readiness.

 - Strong understanding of data center network topologies and high-speed optical connectivity, including transceivers, fiber types, breakout configurations, connector and polarity schemes, and optical loss budgets.

 - Expertise in industry standards such as ANSI/TIA, BICSI and other relevant structured cabling guidelines.

 - Proven ability to coordinate with cross-functional teams and external vendors on large-scale projects.

 - Strong skills in reviewing and interpreting technical drawings, cable schedules, and documentation management.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 - Willingness to travel frequently to global data center sites.

Preferred Skills

 - Master’s degree in Engineering, or relevant certifications such as BICSI, RCDD, or equivalent.

 - Experience with hyperscale cloud, AI, or high-performance computing environments.

 - Proficiency in 2D and 3D engineering tools (e.g., CAD, Revit) for infrastructure design and clash detection analysis.

 - Experience with structured connectivity data and automation for generating and validating port maps, cable schedules, bills of materials, and labels.

 - Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills for physical layer systems and issues.

3336c4da1282.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Applied AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Manager of Applied AI Architects, you will lead a team of senior technical leaders responsible for the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value for OpenAI's largest and most complex customers. Your team will act as the “CTO of the book of business,” partnering with customer executives and technical teams from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable business impact.



You will set the operating model for how Applied AI Architects own technical account plans across ChatGPT Enterprise, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In close partnership with Sales leadership and Account Directors, you will help prioritize customer portfolios, allocate technical resources, and ensure business priorities translate into focused use cases, credible architectures, actionable adoption roadmaps, and durable customer value and growth.



You will remain accountable for the team's technical outcomes while developing its people and bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, research, and partners. You will serve as an executive technical sponsor for critical engagements, a senior voice of the customer inside OpenAI, and a cross-functional leader who can move confidently between regional strategy, executive decision-making, architectural depth, and hands-on coaching.



This role is based in Bangalore.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Hire, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Applied AI Architects, creating an environment of technical excellence, sound judgment, continuous learning, accountability, and strong customer stewardship.

 - Define and continuously refine the strategy and operating model for Applied AI Architecture teams, aligning company priorities with the evolving needs of strategic customers and the regional go-to-market.

 - Partner with Sales leadership and Account Directors to prioritize accounts and opportunities, allocate technical resources effectively, and establish clear technical strategies for the region's most consequential engagements.

 - Ensure Applied AI Architects serve as the primary technical advisors for their portfolios, owning technical account plans, technical milestones, adoption priorities, account health, and expansion opportunities.

 - Lead complex, multi-threaded customer journeys that connect executive vision and business outcomes with use-case qualification, solution evaluation, enterprise governance, and a credible path to production.

 - Coach the team on Applied AI architectures spanning models, applications, data, integration, identity, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, reliability, and deployment.

 - Build trusted relationships with C-suite and board-level stakeholders, as well as senior AI, technology, data, security, and engineering leaders, serving as an executive technical sponsor when needed.

 - Mobilize Deployment Engineering, implementation, enablement, Product, Engineering, Research, Security, Legal, Privacy, partners, and other specialists to remove blockers and deliver a cohesive customer experience.

 - Establish a rigorous view of portfolio health, including technical wins, qualified use cases, production readiness, adoption, usage, risks, measurable customer impact, and the technical contribution to growth.

 - Translate patterns from the field into actionable feedback for Product, Engineering, Research, and go-to-market teams, while developing reusable architecture guidance and customer practices.

 - Foster a culture that balances ambitious customer outcomes with responsible AI deployment, clear ownership, thoughtful prioritization, and effective specialist handoffs.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Possess deep technical acumen in modern AI systems, frontier models, agentic applications, platform technologies, software and cloud architecture, APIs, data integration, identity, security, privacy, evaluation, and enterprise deployment.

 - Bring 10+ years of experience in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, solutions engineering, technical account leadership, AI deployment, or technical consulting, including work with large and complex enterprises.

 - Have 4+ years of people-management experience hiring, coaching, and developing high-performing customer-facing technical teams.

 - Have guided enterprise organizations from technical discovery and evaluation through production adoption, healthy usage, and measurable business impact.

 - Demonstrate outstanding executive communication and presentation skills, with the ability to build credibility with CTOs, CIOs, CISOs, boards, business leaders, and hands-on engineers.

 - Can lead a complex portfolio, make thoughtful resource-allocation decisions, and balance regional strategy with hands-on support for critical customer engagements.

 - Exercise strong architectural judgment, including knowing when to go deep personally, when to coach the team, when to involve specialists, and how to define clear handoffs and ownership.

 - Build strong partnerships across Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, Deployment, Customer Engagement, Security, Legal, Privacy, and external partner ecosystems.

 - Embody a customer-centric philosophy focused on durable value, responsible production adoption, technical excellence, and long-term partnership.

67ca38a6ea40.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s User Operations team shepherds our customers’ adoption of AI and ensures that our customers' product experience is nothing short of exceptional. We are building the very first post-AGI support team. We resolve complex issues, provide technical guidance, and support customers in maximizing value and adoption from deploying our products. We work closely with Sales, Technical Success, Product, Engineering and others, to deliver the best possible experience to our customers at scale. OpenAI's customers represent a range of diverse backgrounds and maturity, from early-stage startups to established global enterprises.

About the Role

The Support Engineering team works closely with Engineering, Product, Technical Success, Go-to-Market, and other teams to deliver an exceptional experience for our most strategic customers. We combine deep technical troubleshooting with durable customer context, proactive reliability work, and clear ownership during critical moments. We use automation, agents, and our own technology to help build the future of technical support.

We’re looking for experienced, deeply curious technical problem-solvers to serve as trusted support partners for our Premium Support customers. You’ll work directly with customers on novel, ambiguous, and high-impact technical issues, using logs, telemetry, reproduction, and systems-level investigation to isolate causes and drive issues toward resolution.

Beyond resolving individual issues, you’ll use your deep understanding of OpenAI’s infrastructure and products, together with each customer’s architecture and operating context, to anticipate risk and make their workloads more resilient over time. You’ll proactively monitor integrations, identify emerging failure patterns and architectural breakpoints, and work with customers and internal teams to address them before they become incidents. Success means that as a customer’s workloads mature and scale, the day-to-day effort required to support them decreases through better monitoring, runbooks, automation, and preventative improvements.

In this role, you will:

 - Work directly with Premium Support customers to troubleshoot their most complex technical issues, including API failures, integration challenges, authentication errors, unexpected product behavior, performance degradation, and production incidents.

 - Provide end-to-end technical ownership by analyzing logs and system behavior, reproducing errors, testing hypotheses, and isolating the likely failure domain. Where possible, you’ll identify the root cause before escalating to Engineering; where that is not possible, you’ll provide a clear hypothesis and the evidence needed to accelerate Engineering’s investigation.

 - Become a trusted expert on OpenAI’s products and systems, serving as a critical escalation point and a technical backstop for our most strategic customers.

 - Own the customer-specific response to high-impact incidents. You’ll assess severity and business impact, initiate the appropriate response path, coordinate cross-functional responders, maintain clear ownership, and ensure issues move through mitigation, resolution, and post-incident follow-through.

 - Communicate clearly and proactively during periods of uncertainty, providing accurate updates to customer technical teams, business stakeholders, executives, and internal partners.

 - Develop a detailed understanding of each customer’s architecture, integrations, dependencies, critical workloads, and operational constraints. You’ll document this context and make it accessible to Support, Product, and Engineering teams.

 - Partner with Go-to-Market and Technical Success teams to understand the business importance of customer workloads and ensure that relevant commercial context informs severity, prioritization, and communication without bypassing established support processes.

 - Represent Support Engineering in relevant customer meetings, including QBRs, and partner closely with account teams to communicate technical health, surface risks and blockers early, coordinate follow-up, and provide customers and internal stakeholders with clear, proactive updates.

 - Monitor customer integrations and support trends to identify emerging risks, recurring failure patterns, and readiness gaps before they become major escalations.

 - Prepare for important launches, migrations, traffic increases, and business events by developing account-specific runbooks, validating escalation paths, coordinating support readiness, and providing heightened monitoring where needed.

 - Lead or contribute to incident reviews and postmortems, identify opportunities to prevent recurrence, and track corrective actions through closure.

 - Translate recurring customer pain into clear, evidence-backed feedback for Product and Engineering, with a particular focus on improving the reliability and performance of existing products, integrations, and deployments.

 - Turn what you learn from customer investigations into scalable improvements, including troubleshooting guides, monitoring, internal tooling, support workflows, and AI-powered automation.

 - Help shape the operating model, technical standards, and tooling for Premium Support as the function grows globally.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have significant experience in Support Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or another role involving hands-on diagnosis of complex production issues.

 - Have expert-level troubleshooting skills and a strong track record of resolving ambiguous technical problems across APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise integrations.

 - Are comfortable working with logs, metrics, traces, API requests, authentication flows, and customer-provided code or configurations to understand system behavior and test hypotheses.

33021fef93dd.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Monetization team is a new cross-functional group spanning engineering, product, research, and design. We are building the foundational systems that will help OpenAI scale access to intelligence responsibly.

Our mission is to create user-first, privacy-preserving monetization products—including next-generation ads experiences—that strengthen trust, expand economic opportunity, and support OpenAI’s long-term innovation. We believe monetization should deliver clear user value, uphold rigorous privacy and safety standards, and sustain a healthy ecosystem for developers and businesses.

The team operates in a greenfield environment, moving quickly through prototyping, experimentation, and iterative deployment. We partner closely across Product, Design, and Research to bring new capabilities into real-world systems at global scale.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an experienced Software Engineer to lead the design and development of the systems that turn advertiser feeds (eg. retail feeds, travel feeds etc.) into relevant, reliably delivered ads. In this foundational role, you will build across the full ads lifecycle—from ingesting and organizing retailer or travel catalogs into efficient retrieval systems, supporting ranking models, and serving ads at scale.

This role is well suited to an engineer with direct experience in product ads retrieval, ranking, and delivery, along with a strong understanding of merchant feeds and shopping systems such as Google Shopping, YouTube product ads, or Amazon. We also welcome engineers with Senior Staff-level or greater scope who have deep ownership of large-scale catalogs, search and indexing, ads serving, or closely related distributed systems.

You will independently own complex systems, make sound technical tradeoffs, and help define the architecture and roadmap for Shopping/Travel/Feed Ads. You will collaborate closely with Ads ML, Ads Delivery, Product, Design, and Research to connect accurate, fresh advertiser feed information with useful ads experiences in ChatGPT.

This role is based in San Francisco and Mountain View. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL

 - Design and build pipelines that ingest, validate, normalize, and refresh merchant product feeds, keeping catalog information accurate and available for serving.

 - Develop scalable catalog storage and indexing systems that make large inventories searchable and reflect changes in product availability, pricing, and attributes.

 - Build search and retrieval systems that efficiently identify relevant, eligible products across merchant catalogs.

 - Partner with Ads ML to connect product retrieval with ranking models through dependable interfaces, features, and serving infrastructure.

 - Engineer low-latency, high-throughput ads delivery systems with strong reliability and correctness guarantees.

 - Design real-time event pipelines and distributed storage that support catalog freshness, serving decisions, and downstream feedback.

 - Build observability and quality controls to detect feed errors, stale inventory, indexing delays, and serving issues.

 - Define technical direction and drive complex projects from early prototypes through production deployment and operation.

 - Operate systems with high engineering rigor through testing, monitoring, privacy and security reviews, and strong operational practices.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - Have extensive experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, with direct ownership of product ads retrieval, ranking infrastructure, or delivery.

 - Understand merchant feeds and shopping systems, including how catalog quality, product availability, and freshness affect relevance and ads performance.

 - Have built systems for shopping or product ads at platforms such as Google Shopping, YouTube, Amazon, or a comparable environment.

 - Alternatively, have operated at Senior Staff-level scope or above, leading the architecture and delivery of large-scale catalogs, search and indexing platforms, ads serving, or related backend systems.

 - Have built low-latency, high-throughput services and data pipelines with demanding reliability and correctness requirements.

 - Can reason across ingestion, storage, indexing, retrieval, ranking, and serving, and make thoughtful tradeoffs between freshness, relevance, latency, and cost.

 - Are comfortable partnering with machine-learning teams to bring ranking models and signals into dependable production systems.

 - Can define technical direction in an ambiguous 0→1 environment and independently drive complex work across teams.

 - Communicate clearly and make technical decisions grounded in user value, merchant experience, and long-term system health.

We want anyone to be able to turn a useful workflow into a plugin, share it, and have other people use it. 4af0fdf258b3.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments and other OpenAI products worldwide. We work across the full funnel—from awareness and acquisition through activation, retention, and expansion—using experimentation, data science, machine learning, and product engineering to help more people discover and realize durable value from OpenAI’s products.

Our team partners closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Design, Finance, Lifecycle, and Growth Marketing. We move quickly, test rigorously, and hold a high bar for measurement, privacy, reliability, and user trust.




ABOUT THIS ROLE: 

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to build the models and decision systems that optimize paid marketing investment for ChatGPT and other OpenAI products. You will develop budget allocation and control algorithms that determine where to invest, how quickly to spend, and how to adjust as performance changes.

The challenge is to make reliable decisions from noisy, delayed, and incomplete signals. You will combine machine learning, optimization, and experimentation to improve incremental growth and long-term user value within budget and efficiency constraints. You will own this work from problem formulation and prototyping through deployment, evaluation, and ongoing operation.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of three days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to eligible employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Build budget allocation algorithms. Decide how to distribute investment across channels, campaigns, and markets using estimates of marginal returns, while accounting for diminishing returns, uncertainty, and business constraints.

 - Develop spend pacing and adaptive control systems. Adjust budgets and spending rates as performance changes, balancing responsiveness with stability when feedback is delayed or noisy. Build in spend limits, monitoring, and safe fallback behavior.

 - Model marketing response and user value. Develop forecasts and models of conversion, long-term value, and saturation that help determine where the next dollar can have the greatest impact.

 - Evaluate decisions rigorously. Use simulations, backtesting, and online experiments to test allocation and control policies. Partner with Data Science to measure incrementality and validate whether offline improvements translate into better investment outcomes.

 - Own reliable production systems. Build data pipelines, training and inference workflows, and integrations that turn model outputs into budget decisions. Establish data-quality checks, monitoring, and retraining with thoughtful treatment of privacy and consent.

 - Turn business goals into optimization problems. Partner with Growth Marketing, Data Science, Engineering, and Finance to define objectives and constraints, communicate tradeoffs, and use evidence to improve investment decisions.

 - Help build a diverse and inclusive culture where people feel welcome, challenge assumptions, and collaborate with candor and respect.




You might thrive in this role if you:

 - 5+ years of experience as a Machine Learning Engineer, Applied Scientist, Data Scientist, or in a comparable quantitative engineering role, or an equivalent record of impact.

 - Experience building and operating production ML or quantitative decision systems, from problem formulation and data pipelines through deployment, experimentation, and monitoring.

 - Strong software engineering skills, proficiency in Python and SQL, and hands-on experience with ML frameworks and large-scale data systems.

 - Strong foundations in machine learning and statistics, with experience applying optimization or control methods to decisions under uncertainty.

 - Experience evaluating models or algorithms with noisy, delayed, or incomplete data, and the judgment to balance model quality, causal impact, and operational reliability.

 - The ability to turn ambiguous goals into focused experiments, interpret mixed results, and communicate clear decisions with technical and non-technical partners.

 - A collaborative working style and a commitment to deploying AI responsibly, in service of OpenAI’s mission to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.

About the Team
OpenAI’s Research Data team exists to accelerate the evaluation, safety and capabilities of our models and products. Made up of technical operators and software engineers, we design the methods through which we acquire and create data.

About the Role
As a Data Program Manager, Science, you will help researchers develop and execute scientific data programs, connecting OpenAI’s research priorities with relevant data, expertise and external partners.

You’ll work closely with researchers to understand their needs, assess the scientific and practical value of opportunities, and develop partnerships across the scientific ecosystem. The work could range from acquiring existing datasets to shaping research collaborations. You’ll carry opportunities from initial investigation through commercial discussions, agreements, delivery and research use, exercising sound judgement around sensitive data and relationships.

Our current work focuses particularly on biology and chemistry. We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ.

In this role, you will:

 - Develop data strategies with Research. Translate research goals, model limitations and evaluation gaps into evidence needs and success criteria. Compare acquisition with internal, public and commissioned alternatives.

 - Find distinctive sources for research. Build trusted local and international relationships across research and industry, including organisations at the scientific frontier.

 - Assess opportunities in scientific context. Inspect samples for provenance, context, quality and completeness. Assess usefulness, involving researchers and specialists as needed.

 - Shape partnerships with lasting scientific value. Understand partners’ ambitions and define pilots, deliverables and acceptance criteria, considering expertise, scientific contribution and continuing relationships alongside commercial terms.

 - Lead commercial and operational execution. Develop proposals, assess pricing and negotiate terms. Coordinate Legal, Privacy, Security, Procurement and engineering to clarify permissions, responsibilities and delivery.

 - Navigate sensitive collaborations. Understand institutional interests and confidentiality. Identify ethical, privacy, security and misuse concerns early, involving specialists to develop responsible arrangements.

 - Follow through into research use. Coordinate preparation, ingestion, access and documentation. Gather researcher feedback to inform whether to expand, change or stop.

 - Make thoughtful portfolio decisions. Recommend options based on research value, cost, timing and capacity. Identify shared needs and opportunities for useful collaboration across projects.

 - Make the work more repeatable. Use code, APIs, automation and AI tools to improve sourcing, assessment and delivery. Resolve recurring blockers with engineers and retain partner knowledge and research feedback.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have substantial grounding in biology, chemistry or related sciences through research, industry or equivalent experience, and engage critically with methods and evidence.

 - Have delivered complex scientific, data or partnership projects, with depth in one or more of scientific data and evaluation, commercial partnerships or research collaborations across organisations.

 - Exercise sound judgement: test claims, match evidence to research needs and make clear recommendations while acknowledging uncertainty.

 - Work directly with data: inspect unfamiliar files, investigate quality and use Python, SQL, APIs and AI-assisted coding to answer questions and reduce manual work.

 - Build trust through careful listening, precise questions and thoughtful negotiation. You bring relevant local and international relationships, or a demonstrated ability to develop them, and understand what partners value beyond the transaction.

 - Exercise discretion, recognising the limits of your expertise and authority and when scientific, ethical or safety questions need specialist input.

 - Thrive in a fast-moving environment, taking broad ownership across multiple projects and moving readily between scientific, technical and commercial questions. You prioritise thoughtfully as needs change, making clear decisions about where to focus and what can wait.

 - Enjoy getting your hands dirty, bringing energy and creative problem solving to unfamiliar or ambiguous opportunities. You turn them into practical plans and follow through on the details.

 - Learn exceptionally quickly, developing your understanding of AI training, evaluation and unfamiliar research areas to become a useful collaborator.

 - We welcome different combinations of scientific, technical and partnership experience. You do not need equal depth in every area.

c79771135941.title: Software Engineer, HSM Infrastructure Security, Consumer Devices
c79771135941.description:
We are hiring a Security Software Engineer to design and implement the hardware-backed security foundations used across OpenAI’s device ecosystem.



A central focus of this role is hardening the boundary between our policy systems and the HSMs that protect sensitive cryptographic keys. This boundary determines which operations may be performed, what may be signed, which policies must be satisfied, and how changes to trusted software and policy are authorized.



You will develop security-critical software and firmware within, or immediately adjacent to, an HSM trust boundary. Depending on your background, this may include HSM trusted applications, firmware services, cryptographic mechanisms, device drivers, PKCS#11 components, secure-provisioning protocols, or signing-policy enforcement systems.



This is a hands-on software-engineering role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review production code, debug across hardware and software boundaries, and carry projects from initial requirements through deployment. It is not an HSM administration, PKI operations, compliance, or architecture-only position.



In This Role, You Will

 - Design and implement security-critical software and firmware for HSMs, secure elements, trusted execution environments, and hardware roots of trust.

 - Build and harden the policy-to-HSM boundary responsible for authorizing certificate issuance and cryptographic signing operations.

 - Develop HSM trusted applications, firmware components, host interfaces, device drivers, SDKs, or cryptographic service integrations.

 - Implement or extend cryptographic interfaces such as PKCS#11, OpenSSL providers or engines, platform key-storage APIs, or comparable hardware-security interfaces.

 - Build firmware and software that cryptographically enforces key generation, provisioning, usage, rotation, recovery, and destruction policies.

 - Design and implement HSM-backed certificate authority, code-signing, key-management, and device-identity systems.

 - Develop end-to-end cryptographic protocols spanning devices, secure hardware, policy services, and backend infrastructure.

 - Build security capabilities supporting device attestation, secure boot, factory provisioning and restoration, user registration, and authentication.

 - Design controls that make trusted software and policy changes verifiable, auditable, and subject to appropriate multi-party authorization.

 - Write, review, test, and audit secure embedded software for resource-constrained environments.

 - Develop test harnesses, emulators, fuzzers, and fault-injection tooling to validate security properties and failure behavior.

 - Threat-model hardware and software trust boundaries and translate findings into concrete engineering improvements.

 - Partner with hardware, firmware, infrastructure, application, and security teams to integrate secure-by-default capabilities into production systems.

 - Help establish engineering standards for HSM development, applied cryptography, secure key management, and certificate infrastructure.



Minimum Qualifications

 - 5+ years experience building secure embedded firmware for constrained environments

 - Deep programming experience in C, C++, or Rust.



You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

 - A strong track record of designing, implementing, debugging, and shipping production systems software.

 - Hands-on experience developing security-critical software or firmware within, or directly adjacent to, an HSM, secure element, TEE, or hardware root of trust.

 - Experience developing one or more of the following:
   
   - HSM firmware or trusted applications
   
   - Cryptographic mechanisms or hardware-accelerated cryptographic services
   
   - HSM device drivers, host libraries, SDKs, or middleware
   
   - PKCS#11 providers, mechanisms, or integrations
   
   - Secure key-provisioning or key-injection protocols
   
   - HSM-backed certificate authority or code-signing systems
   
   - Signing-policy enforcement within a hardware-backed trust boundary

 - Strong knowledge of applied cryptography, digital signatures, key hierarchies, secure key management, and cryptographic protocol design.

 - Experience with PKI, X.509 certificates, certificate authorities, certificate issuance, and certificate lifecycle protocols.

 - Familiarity with secure boot, measured boot, device identity, remote attestation, or hardware-backed storage.

 - Experience reasoning about concurrency, memory safety, privilege separation, hardware interfaces, failure modes, and side-channel or physical attack considerations.

 - The ability to evaluate security designs and personally implement the software required to realize them.

 - Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate across hardware, firmware, backend, and product teams.



Additional Experience That May Be Helpful

 - Firmware development for ARM TrustZone or another trusted execution environment.

 - Experience with commercial or cloud HSM platforms such as Thales Luna, Entrust/nShield, Utimaco, Marvell LiquidSecurity, AWS CloudHSM, or comparable systems.

 - Experience with PKCS#11, KMIP, OpenSSL providers or engines, secure-element APIs, or platform-native key-storage frameworks.

 - Device manufacturing, secure provisioning, factory restore, or silicon bring-up experience.

 - Secure boot ROM, bootloader, firmware-signing, anti-rollback, or authenticated-update development.

 - Developing trusted applications or cryptographic services inside an HSM or secure coprocessor.

 - Hardware/software co-design involving cryptographic accelerators, secure processors, or custom silicon.

 - Multi-party authorization, quorum-controlled deployments, tamper-resistant audit mechanisms, or attestable policy systems.

 - Secure or private storage systems based on hardware-protected keys.

 - Experience sustaining high-assurance security software in production.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Browser Use team builds the technology that enables agents to interact with browsers across our products. Our work spans infrastructure, tooling, and user experiences, both on users’ devices and in the cloud. We partner with research to improve our models’ browser-use capabilities and with web standards bodies to shape how agents interact with the web. Our products include ChatGPT for Chrome, the ChatGPT in-app browser, and the cloud computer used in dots and ChatGPT Work.


We see the browser as a universal connector. If we can enable our models to use it effectively, they can do anything. Come help us build the future of browsing!




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a product-oriented engineer to build and scale our cloud computer infrastructure. Our goal is to give every one of our users access to an agent with their own computer in the cloud. Build novel solutions to problems like authentication, user takeover, and enterprise network access. You’ll help own the systems that provision, run, and manage the environments our agents use, making them reliable, responsive, and efficient as demand grows.


This role combines infrastructure depth with close attention to the user experience. You’ll partner with research and engineering teams to bring new computer-use capabilities into production, working across container orchestration, backend services, and product experiences.




IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL

 - Build and scale infrastructure for running agent-controlled browsers and computers in the cloud.

 - Develop services for provisioning environments, managing sessions, and coordinating their lifecycle.

 - Improve reliability, performance, resource utilization, and observability across the fleet.

 - Diagnose issues across Linux, containers, networking, and browser execution.

 - Build APIs and tooling that make cloud computers easy for research and product teams to use.

 - Work closely with research to understand emerging requirements and improve how computer use works.

 - Develop authentication, credential management, and network access controls that protect user data and support interactions with websites and services.

 - Experience leading large-scale backend, platform, or infrastructure projects from ambiguous problem statements to production systems.

 - Proficiency in one or more backend languages such as Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, or similar, and the ability to move across service, platform, and product boundaries.

 - Strong understanding of distributed systems, cloud platforms, and production reliability.

 - Own systems from initial design through deployment and scale.

 - Comfort with a fast-moving pace while caring for security and operational excellence.



Experience with browser automation, remote computing environments, or infrastructure for AI agents would be especially relevant.

811fead7cbc2.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.

Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.

You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in Munich. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

In this role, you will:

 - Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

 - Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

 - Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

 - Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

 - Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.

 - Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.

 - Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.

 - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, product engineering or technical consulting.

 - Are fluent in both German and English

 - Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or engineering of production systems—not only program or stakeholder management.

 - Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

 - Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.

 - Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

 - Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

 - Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

 - Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.

 - Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.

3a4ff5ebedb9.title: SoC Engineer
3a4ff5ebedb9.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops custom silicon and systems for advanced AI workloads. Our first-party accelerator team works across chip architecture, design, software, and systems to build the computing platforms that power frontier models. We are a small, dynamic team that values technical breadth, hands-on engineering, and creative approaches to building complex hardware.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a SoC Engineer to help architect, design, and integrate OpenAI’s first-party AI accelerators. You will build the processor, interconnect, I/O, and platform infrastructure that connects our accelerator designs into complete, functional systems.

This role combines architectural judgment with hands-on implementation. You’ll work closely with design, architecture, verification, and software teams throughout development, from defining subsystem requirements and integrating IP to pre-silicon validation, silicon bring-up, and post-silicon debug. You should enjoy stretching across domains, rolling up your sleeves, and doing the work needed to make a complex system function end to end.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Define and implement SoC architectures spanning embedded processors, AMBA interconnects, peripheral subsystems, PCI Express, Ethernet and die-to-die interfaces.

 - Develop the microarchitecture and RTL design of subsystems supporting I/O and SoC functionality.

 - Integrate Arm Cortex-M and Cortex-A processors, AXI/APB fabrics, and third-party controller IP, including the RTL and glue logic needed to connect these components.

 - Develop reset and boot architectures, working with firmware and software teams to define sequencing, initialization, and survivability behavior.

 - Incorporate debug, test, and security requirements into the SoC architecture and implementation, partnering with other silicon designers to make the silicon observable, testable, and secure.

 - Drive PCIe and other I/O integration, including controller and PHY interfaces, high-speed SerDes, and die-to-die connectivity.

 - Contribute to power management and security architecture and design.

 - Work directly with third-party IP vendors to define technical requirements, evaluate IP capabilities, coordinate deliverables, and resolve issues from integration through silicon bring-up.

 - Work across architecture, design, verification, physical design, and software teams to define interfaces, resolve integration issues, and carry designs through pre-silicon validation and post-silicon bring-up.

 - Work closely with Firmware and Software teams to define boot, configuration and runtime behavior and functionality.

 - Build and apply automation and AI-assisted tools to accelerate design, IP integration, consistency checking, and debugging while maintaining engineering quality.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have experience in SoC architecture, RTL design, and subsystem or full-chip integration, with hands-on ownership through implementation and silicon bring-up.

 - Are familiar with Arm processor subsystems, including Cortex-M and Cortex-A, and AMBA protocols and interconnects such as AXI and APB.

 - Understand PCIe protocols and have experience configuring, integrating, and debugging controller IP.

 - Have experience integrating high-speed I/O, including SerDes/PHY interfaces and die-to-die links.

 - Have experience working directly with third-party IP vendors to evaluate technical fit, communicate requirements, and drive integration and debug issues to resolution.

 - Understand reset and boot architecture and the interactions between hardware, firmware, and software during initialization and recovery.

 - Have experience designing for debug, test, and security, and can reason about how these requirements affect the broader system.

 - Are comfortable writing and debugging Verilog/SystemVerilog and building scripts or tools to make integration work more efficient and reliable.

 - Enjoy stretching into multiple domains, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and rolling up your sleeves to build and debug.

 - Enjoy working on a small, dynamic team where priorities evolve and engineers take broad ownership.

 - Are excited about creatively applying automation and AI tools to hardware design and integration work.

To comply with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidates for this role may need to meet certain legal status requirements as provided in those laws and regulations.

About the Team

Identity is the foundation of trust in an AI-powered world. As people build a rich personal and organizational context in ChatGPT, they need systems that protect it, remember it, and let them share it securely across apps and agents. Without strong identity, context stays locked away or exposed. With it, AI becomes safe, personal, and truly useful, empowering users while keeping control firmly in their hands. Our team builds the trusted OpenAI account layer that connects people, enterprises, developers, and agents to OpenAI apps and the broader AI ecosystem. Our systems are the front door to OpenAI—held to an exceptionally high bar for availability, security, and latency—and are depended on by many internal teams.

About the Role

As an Engineering Manager, Identity Platform you will lead a team owning foundational identity services that must be highly reliable, secure, and fast under extreme load. You’ll set direction, grow and support the team, and partner closely across engineering and security to strengthen the platform that enables trusted access to OpenAI products.

In this role, you will:

 - Build, lead, and develop a high-performing engineering team. Coach and mentor engineers and senior technical leads to increase their impact and support their growth.

 - Define and own the technical strategy, roadmap, and execution for OpenAI’s core identity systems.

 - Guide the architecture of distributed systems operating at massive scale, with high requirements for reliability, privacy, and performance.

 - Partner closely with Product and Infrastructure teams to support new product needs and uphold high system standards.

 - Ensure the team operates effectively, maintains strong engineering rigor, and consistently delivers against ambitious goals.

 - Establish processes and a culture that enable fast learning, high trust, and responsible innovation.

 - Lead the team responsible for the authentication stack and token exchange infrastructure, ensuring high availability, strong security posture, and low-latency performance.

 - Own and improve request validation at the edge for logged-in users, delivering extremely high reliability and fast validation under high throughput.

 - Oversee systems that enable secure access to user data, improving scalability, reliability, and access patterns for internal consumers across the company.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 10+ years of experience building, scaling, and operating distributed systems at large scale.

 - Have 3+ years of experience managing high-performance engineering teams in fast-paced, rapidly shifting environments.

 - Care deeply about people leadership, coaching, and helping engineers achieve peak performance.

 - Communicate clearly, think holistically, and make decisions grounded in both user needs and long-term sustainability.

 - Have experience managing an infrastructure team and are effective at hiring, coaching, and developing engineers while maintaining strong operational excellence.

 - Have deep experience building and operating high-scale backend systems, with a track record of improving reliability, latency, and security in production.

About the Team

Enterprise Security protects the systems, identities, devices, and services that enable OpenAI's employees to work securely and effectively. We partner across IT and Security to understand risk, build practical defenses, and support a rapidly evolving technical environment.

In this role, you’d have an opportunity to build this system from the ground up. You’d be a key contributor, working on a problem few teams have had to solve at this scale.

 - Strong storage fundamentals, including replication, consistency, caching, and data lifecycle management.

 - Strong coding ability. We work in Python and Go; experience in either is enough, but you should be willing to pick up the other

 - Experience with parallel or HPC filesystems such as Weka, VAST, or Lustre.

You will own the cohesive vision of these tooling repositories.

You will work closely with a team of research scientists and engineers to create tooling that enables tighter experimentation cycles, better data coverage of the real world, and more scientific rigour. You will have a lot of autonomy and need to be opinionated about what areas of the codebase need elegance and standards, and where that would be overengineering. You will be given high level experimental problems that need to be solved with efficient pipelines, and design and implement the solutions. Your data analysis will collaboratively feed into modelling decisions and experimentation.

This role combines expertise in software engineering, statistics, and data science. If any of these topics sound interesting to you, we encourage you to apply.

You will be working on the Modelling Safety and Trust team, so interest in these areas is a plus, but is not at all required.

Please Note: We have offices in London, Edinburgh, Paris, Toronto, Montreal and New York, but we also embrace being remote-friendly! This role has timezone restrictions (UK, Europe, or ET) but no location restrictions.

 - Collaborate with the ML modeling team to align data capabilities with experimental needs

 - Maintain opinionated, well-documented solutions that become team standards

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

Why this role?

We are on a mission to build machines that understand the world and make them safely accessible to all. Data quality is foundational to this process. Machines (or Large Language Models, to be exact) learn in similar ways to humans, by way of feedback. By labelling, ranking, auditing, and correcting model output, you will improve Large Language Models' performance for iterations to come, thus having a lasting impact on Cohere's technology. We are hiring Generalist professionals with broad backgrounds that span multiple consumer-facing or personal domains.

This is a judgment-driven role, not passive data entry. You will review, assess, and provide structured feedback across a broad and evolving range of tasks, evaluating, stress-testing, and improving our models on English-language data spanning multiple modalities (text, image, and structured formats such as JSON, CSV/TSV, and Markdown). This is a great opportunity for professionals with strong analytical skills to contribute to high-impact annotation projects.

Please Note: This is a part-time independent contractor position available within Canada only. We seek candidates who can commit to 16 hours per week at a CAD $30/hour contract rate. This role is BYOD 💻 (Bring Your Own Device, laptop). This position is remote.

As an Data Annotation Specialist, you will:

 - Evaluate and rank model outputs: Complete preference and comparison tasks, assessing which responses best conform to project guidelines for accuracy, helpfulness, tone, and safety, and writing clear justifications for your judgments.

 - Stress-test and break models: Probe models adversarially to surface failure modes, unsafe behavior, and capability gaps, and document reproducible cases that engineering and research teams can act on.

 - Create datasets: Author high-quality prompts, responses, and exemplars to build training and evaluation datasets, following detailed specifications and editing machine-written or human-written outputs to standard.

 - Build and apply rubrics and taxonomies: Contribute to the design of grading criteria and rubrics, then apply them consistently to produce structured, high-quality annotations across task types.

 - Annotate and correct multimodal data: Label, audit, and rectify inaccuracies across text, image, and structured data, maintaining a high standard of data integrity and accuracy.

 - Calibrate and maintain consistency: Participate in calibration exercises and inter-annotator agreement checks to align on standards, and flag ambiguous or uncovered edge cases rather than guessing, since a single misjudgment replicated at scale degrades a model.

 - Adapt to experimental work: Take on new and evolving task types as project needs shift, applying sound judgment in areas where guidelines are still being developed.

 - Report on model performance: Surface and communicate quality and performance trends in model and agent behavior, giving cross-functional partners clear, well-evidenced feedback on where models succeed, fail, and degrade.

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - 1+ years of experience in AI data annotation, LLM evaluation, content moderation, research, or a related analytical role, with exposure to quality assurance, and/or preference ranking.

 - Experience applying detailed guidelines to complex and often ambiguous content, with strong contextual and sociocultural judgment, sensitivity to nuance, tone, and register, and the ability to reason well in cases where there is no single correct answer.

 - Comfort with ambiguity: a willingness to flag unclear or uncovered edge cases rather than guess, and to work productively on novel, experimental tasks whose definitions are still evolving.

 - A sharp, curious eye for inconsistencies, subtle errors, and model failure modes, including the instinct to probe models adversarially and surface where they break. Familiarity with how large language models behave, such as hallucination, sycophancy, and instruction-following gaps, is a plus.

 - Excellent command of written English and strong reading comprehension, with the ability to clearly justify your evaluations, including why an output is correct or incorrect, high-quality or low-quality, and to write clear prompts and exemplars that explain your reasoning. Bonus points if you are fluent in another language!

 - Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy, with the ability to maintain consistency across high-volume and monotonous tasks.

 - Comfort working with annotation platforms and structured formats such as JSON, CSV/TSV, Markdown, XML, and YAML.

 - Strong execution in a remote environment, including good time management, comfort using new tools, and the ability to work independently in a global, asynchronous team.

Candidate Journey

 - First Assessment: If selected to move forward, you’ll receive a multiple-choice assessment by email.

 - Help other engineers add integrations of their own, and raise the bar for how the team does it.

 - Create evals and tests to make sure integrations work as expected and alert on regressions.

 - Tune tool descriptions to improve performance based on feedback and evals.

 - Use AI actively in your work, while staying accountable for the quality and reliability of what you ship.

 - You have shipped production code and are comfortable building integrations against external APIs.

 - You excel in fast-paced environments and can execute while priorities are a moving target.

 - You bring high agency: you learn quickly and drive change without waiting for perfect instructions.

 - You've owned things end-to-end before and care about the quality of what ships, not just that it shipped.
