19753684ecd1.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is responsible for building the next generation of AI-native silicon while working closely with software and research partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering production-grade silicon for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team also creates custom design tools and methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable hardware optimized specifically for AI.

The Compute team works on the design of our AI supercomputers, doing everything from workload modeling to influencing accelerator design. We’re leaning into our partnerships to make system and data center co-design an integral part of this process, and are looking for engineers to design AI supercomputers solutions for data center applications

This team is responsible for working with partners to optimize their hardware for our workloads, identifying promising new deep learning accelerators, and bringing those hardware platforms to production.

If you’re excited to work at the intersection of cutting edge deep learning, hardware system, and data center design this role is for you!

About the Role

We’re looking for a Product Reliability Engineer to own reliability engineering for advanced IT hardware, from printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) through compute and networking trays, systems, and fully integrated racks. You’ll translate operating conditions and service-life goals into reliability requirements, design and execute qualification tests, and drive failure analysis and corrective-action verification from development through production and field deployment. Working with electrical, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, quality, and data center teams, suppliers, and manufacturing partners, you’ll use test and field evidence to improve hardware durability, serviceability, and availability.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Define reliability requirements and targets for PCBAs, trays, systems, and racks using mission profiles, expected service life, operating environments, duty cycles, and availability goals.

 - Drive design-for-reliability reviews with electrical, mechanical, and thermal engineers. Use failure modes and effects analysis (DFMEA or FMEA) and physics of failure to prioritize risks and recommend design improvements. Own component de-rating guidelines and guidance.

 - Own reliability qualification plans from new product introduction through production, defining test coverage, representative configurations, sample sizes, stress conditions, duration, pass/fail criteria, and exit evidence at each assembly level.

 - Develop and execute accelerated life and environmental tests, including temperature cycling, humidity exposure, power cycling, shock, vibration, and transport testing. Exercise hardware under representative workloads and monitor function and degradation during stress.

 - Analyze life-test and field data using Weibull and other reliability models, acceleration models, and confidence intervals. State assumptions, exposure, and uncertainty when estimating failure rates, useful life, or reliability against targets.

 - Lead failure investigations from symptom reproduction through physical root cause. Maintain failure reporting, analysis, and corrective-action records, and verify fixes through targeted testing and recurrence monitoring.

 - Review supplier reliability plans and evidence for PCBs, PCBa components/assemblies, cables, connectors, and cooling components. Identify gaps between component qualification and the stresses encountered in the integrated system or rack.

 - Work hands-on with internal and partner labs to develop fixtures, instrumentation, and test methods. Review sample traceability, test configurations, calibration, raw data, and failure capture, including on-site support at manufacturing partners.

 - Partner with manufacturing and quality engineers to establish and validate reliability screens, burn-in where justified, and ongoing reliability testing. Confirm screening detects relevant defects without consuming unacceptable product life.

 - Evaluate reliability risks introduced by assembly and integration: board strain and solder-joint damage, connector mating and retention, cable routing, fastener preload, power connections, and thermal interfaces. Partner with cooling specialists on leak integrity, material compatibility, corrosion, and cooling performance over life.

 - Plan reliability test resources, lab capacity, hardware samples, schedules, and dependencies across programs with engineering teams, technical program managers, suppliers, and manufacturing partners.

 - Present qualification results, unresolved failure modes, and residual risk at design and release reviews. Make evidence-based readiness recommendations and clearly identify test gaps, required follow-up, and decisions for accountable owners.

 - Assess reliability impact and define targeted requalification for design, component, supplier, manufacturing process, and repair changes, including firmware changes that alter hardware operating stresses.

 - Track field returns and fleet failure trends with service and data center teams. Correlate telemetry, failure analysis, and configuration history to prioritize corrective actions and feed lessons into future designs and qualification plans.

 - Validate serviceability and repeated assembly or maintenance operations, including connector mating cycles and component replacement. Work with system engineers to assess how hardware failures, redundancy, and recovery affect rack availability.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have hands-on reliability engineering experience with advanced IT hardware, such as AI/H

We're seeking an experienced Program Manager to join Cohere's customer-facing Program Management team, with a focus on public sector and defence accounts in Europe, particularly in Germany. This is a highly specialised role requiring an individual who understands technical program delivery, the technical complexity of frontier AI models and the unique requirements of government and defence organisations.

You will be the critical bridge between our cutting-edge AI capabilities and the specific needs of Ministries, Agencies, and defence organisations across Europe. You'll navigate complex procurement processes, stringent security requirements, data sovereignty concerns, and regulatory compliance while ensuring our customers successfully deploy and scale our AI solutions.

In this role, you'll collaborate with our Strategic Customer team, Applied ML (AML) Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), Platform, Product, and Go-to-Market teams, serving as the technical program lead and trusted advisor for our most sensitive and high-impact government and defence engagements.

Location: Germany

WHO WE ARE

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.



Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

As a Developer Platform https://www.notion.com/product/dev engineer, you will directly contribute to the foundational pieces that make Notion extensible and connected. You will build tools, APIs, and platform experiences that help customers connect Notion to the world — bringing their apps, data, and workflows into one workspace. Your work will make it easier for developers, admins, and builders to create reliable integrations and automations on top of Notion.


You will be a key player in building the robust technical foundation that allows Notion to achieve the connected workspace vision. Your work will include both internal platform contributions that accelerate other Notion engineering teams and end-user-facing functionality that enables toolmaking ubiquity. You will be presented with challenging technical problems, as Notion’s product needs are complex. You’ll play a key role in identifying and executing against technical investments that ensure the long-term quality, reliability, and performance of Notion’s platform as we scale.


This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

 - You’ll work with a team of engineers and cross-functional partners across product, design, data science, and user research to define a product strategy and drive execution through conception, research, implementation, and maintenance.

 - You’ll evolve Developer Platform capabilities across APIs, MCP tools, and integration infrastructure that help customers automate workflows, customize Notion, and connect Notion to the tools and data they use every day.

 - You’ll contribute to the overall performance, reliability, and robustness of the Notion product, ensuring it scales elegantly across many dimensions.

 - You’ll partner with engineering leaders to identify and execute against high-leverage technical investments that ensure the long-term flexibility and sustainability of our core systems.

 - 7+ years of experience shipping production software, with a strong track record of owning features end-to-end

 - Fluency with TypeScript across both backend and frontend

 - Strong product instincts: you can take a vague problem, propose a solid technical approach, and know when to cut scope

 - You don’t need to be an AI expert, but you’re curious and willing to adopt AI tools to work smarter and deliver better results




NICE TO HAVES:

 - Experience building developer tools like APIs and SDKs

 - Experience driving teams toward shared goals and balancing business priorities with individuals’ strengths, areas of interest, and career development goals

 - Familiarity with AI/agent tooling, evals, or LLM-driven product experiences



Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role’s scope and complexity, and the candidate’s experience and expertise, and may vary from the range provided below. For roles based in San Francisco or New York City, the estimated base salary range for this role is $179,000 – $200,000 per year.

f9760d98a833.description:
ABOUT US



At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.

With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.

Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.






ABOUT THE TEAM

The LangSmith team owns and builds LangChain's core platform for observability, evaluation, and production reliability of AI systems. From tracing and annotation to run rules, evaluations, and beyond, this team owns LangSmith end-to-end. If you want to define what great AI observability looks like at production scale, this is where that work gets done.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the team building LangSmith, our observability and evaluation platform for LLM applications. You’ll define the technical direction, grow and mentor a world-class engineering team, and partner with product and design to deliver features that help developers build and deploy trustworthy AI systems with confidence.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build, mentor, and grow a high-performing team of engineers, fostering collaboration, ownership, and accountability

 - Strengthen LangChain’s engineering culture through mentorship, high-quality code, and technical excellence

 - Shape long-term technical direction and ensure scalability and reliability of LangSmith AI Observability Platform

 - Partner with product and design teams to define scope, sequence, and success criteria for key initiatives

 - Maintain a high bar for technical excellence while making sure the team moves with urgency and focus

 - Lead by example in writing clean, maintainable, and well-tested code in Go/Python and Typescript

 - Engage directly with customers to understand their needs and translate them into actionable product improvements




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Experience managing or tech-leading teams delivering complex full-stack products

 - Strong technical background in Go/Python and React/Typescript

 - Solid understanding of databases (Postgres, Redis and ClickHouse)

 - Proven ability to design high throughput data-intensive systems

 - Bias towards shipping quickly and learning from customers

 - Strong communication skills—able to collaborate with internal stakeholders and engage directly with customers

 - Bonus: Experience building AI/LLM-powered applications, developer tools, or observability platforms



 - Annual salary range: $200,000- $250,000

Compensation Philosophy:

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. 

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.




BENEFITS

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

5aee8e3262d4.title: Software Engineer, Internship - Query Engines
5aee8e3262d4.description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.


The Role
We are a software engineering team applying open-source data technologies to some of the world's hardest and most important problems. We build the data processing infrastructure that underpins Palantir Foundry, supporting applications that help hospitals care for more patients, help clinical teams coordinate timely diagnoses, and keep essential supplies moving through global disruption.
 
You will work deep inside the systems that make this possible: how computations are represented, how query plans are optimised, how operators execute, and how data is read and written efficiently. We build on and extend Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, and Apache Iceberg, bringing advances in open-source engines and table formats into the demanding environments our customers operate in. Our work serves many products and workloads across Foundry, including no-code pipelines, interactive analysis, and the processing that keeps the Ontology up to date.
 
Working alongside experienced engineers, you will take on real problems in our production systems. That could mean writing a new planning rule, adding a capability to a native execution engine, or making large tables faster to scan. You will see your work through design, code review, testing, and release. Correctness, compatibility, and predictable performance are central to everything we build, and you will learn how to deliver all three.
 
Join us if you want to learn how modern data systems work from the inside and apply that knowledge to consequential problems.

Technologies We Use
Java, Scala, Rust, and Python Apache Spark, Apache DataFusion, Apache Comet, and Velox for data processing and query execution Apache Iceberg for table management and catalog interoperability Apache Arrow and Apache Parquet for in-memory data processing and columnar storage Gradle and Cargo for builds, and GitHub for collaboration You do not need prior experience with these technologies. We expect you to learn them here.
What We Value
Curiosity about how data systems work, from query optimisers and execution operators to file formats and distributed processing A high bar for correctness and a willingness to dig until you understand why something behaves the way it does Comfort following a problem across languages, services, and layers of the stack A practical approach to performance, grounded in measurement rather than intuition Eagerness to learn, ask questions, and incorporate feedback Interest in applying deep systems engineering to real-world problems, with empathy for the people who depend on our software
What We Require
Currently pursuing or recently completed a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, or a similar field, or equivalent practical experience Proficiency in at least one language such as Java, Rust, Scala, C++, or C Strong foundations in algorithms, data structures, and concurrency Strong written and verbal communication skills Coursework or projects in databases, compilers, operating systems, or distributed systems Contributions to open-source projects Must be planning on graduating in 2028. This should be your final internship before graduating.
Salary
The estimated salary range for this position is estimated to be $10,500/month. Further note that total compensation for this position will be determined by each individual’s relevant qualifications, work experience, skills, and other factors. This estimate excludes the value of any benefits offered; and the potential future value of any long-term incentives.


Life at Palantir
 
We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
 
In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.
 
If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process, please reach out and let us know how we can help.
 
Please note that you will never be asked to submit a payment or share financial information to participate in our interview process. If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

075454641faf.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is looking for a Staff+ Software Engineer to work on the vector search infrastructure behind Claude. Retrieval is how Claude learns about the world. Web search across claude.ai, the API and agentic surfaces, memory across conversations, and the reinforcement learning workloads that train our next models all depend on fast, cheap, high-recall nearest-neighbor search over billions of vectors. You'll join a small team responsible for the vector database layer that serves Claude's retrieval workloads: its architecture, performance, scalability and cost. This is a foundational role. The team is small, core architectural decisions are still open, and the engineers who join now will shape how the system evolves. The role sits in our Databases organization and works day to day with the Search Platform team, which owns web search indexing, retrieval and serving, and the Memory & Search team, which owns search and memory inside claude.ai. We're looking for someone who has built vector or search systems that ran in production, at scale, with real users and a real on-call. You'll be hands-on in the code, and you'll also be the person deciding how the pieces fit together. Key responsibilities Own the core of Anthropic's vector database layer: index structures, storage layout, query execution and the serving layer Own production readiness - benchmarking against exact search, capacity planning, onboarding new workloads, and the operational tooling to run it at scale Drive the recall, latency and cost trade-offs - quantization, filtered search, index build and refresh strategy, and how compute and storage are separated and scaled Scale throughput by an order of magnitude as research and training demand grows, and work out whether the bottleneck is architecture, hardware or engineering bandwidth Extend the retrieval stack toward hybrid retrieval - lexical search and fused ranking alongside vector search Set the evaluation methodology for the system - recall targets, latency objectives, cost per query, and the regression detection that keeps them honest Set technical direction for a growing team - lead design reviews, make architectural decisions others build on, and mentor the engineers joining the effort Share the on-call for the systems you own Minimum qualifications Direct experience building a vector database or approximate nearest-neighbor search system that ran in production at scale Deep knowledge of ANN index structures (graph-based, clustering-based or disk-resident approaches), vector quantization and filtered search Experience with search relevance and ranking Strong systems programming skills in a language such as Rust, C++ or Go, including performance-critical and memory-intensive code Experience designing and operating large-scale distributed storage or serving systems with strict latency and reliability requirements A track record of independently scoping and delivering ambiguous, multi-quarter technical projects Strong written and verbal communication, with experience driving alignment across teams with different priorities Interest in AI safety and Anthropic's mission Preferred qualifications Experience with object-storage-backed or disaggregated compute and storage database designs Experience building or operating full-text search engines (inverted indexes, BM25) or hybrid retrieval systems Familiarity with embedding models and the retrieval demands of LLM training and inference Experience using GPUs or other accelerators for index build or search Prior experience as a technical lead on a database or search infrastructure team The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. Think on your feet and communicate technical concepts, explaining how Stripe works from both a product feature and API architecture perspective. Apply AI across the engagement lifecycle to reduce manual effort, accelerate delivery, and improve the quality of what we hand to users. Ability to write code (in programming languages like Go, Java, C/C++ etc.) and quickly debug user code snippets. Comfortable with various code-level debugging (Stripe code and user code) and using code as a tool for problem-solving. Strong generalist technical experience, including proficiency in SQL and an understanding of data structures and algorithms. Understanding of the payments domain and API security topics. Be comfortable talking about technical concepts, and explaining how Stripe works, both from a product features and API architecture perspective. A user first approach & empathy with our users, capable of mapping business requirements into reliable technical solutions. Confident and comfortable with customers, with the ability to lead strategic technical conversations. Hands-on experience using AI tools (e.g. coding assistants, LLM-based agents) to improve how you work, and a strong appetite to continue to build that experience quickly. Preferred qualifications Enjoy the puzzle of solving open-ended problems, both individually and as a member of our team. Willingness to learn and teach others, including mentoring newer team members. Collaborative, communicative, consultative; able to apply specific methodologies to ensure repeatability of engagements. Intellectually curious, with great problem solving skills. Technical writing skills to document complex integration guidance and processes.

Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team The IAM Control Plane team’s mission is to empower Stripe users to easily and securely manage their access to Stripe products and data. As part of Stripe's Organizations and Auth Platform, we own the platform for API keys, user roles, and access auditing, ensuring the right people have the keys to the kingdom - and no one else. We are a team of around 10 engineers with an ambitious roadmap, blending deep platform work with direct product impact. What you’ll do You will design, build, and maintain the critical systems that control our user’s access to Stripe. Responsibilities Design and build the next generation of IAM primitives to securely power AI-driven agentic experiences on Stripe Develop new user-facing permission models, including custom roles and granular access controls Architect and implement platform features like Account Groups to simplify access management for large organizations Own and operate mission-critical, highly-available backend services that are fundamental to every Stripe user's experience Work across the stack to ship end-to-end features, from API design and database modeling to frontend components Improve engineering standards, tooling, and processes as well as mentor team members Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 2762c01920fe.description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About the team Radar helps businesses prevent payments fraud and abuse while enabling legitimate customers to transact with confidence. We combine machine learning and AI with the intelligence of Stripe’s global network to make sophisticated fraud prevention accessible to businesses of all sizes. Our work spans payments fraud detection, protection against abuse beyond the payment, enterprise APIs that bring Radar’s capabilities into businesses’ own systems and payment flows, and the platform that powers it all. We build everything from reliable, low-latency infrastructure to intuitive tools that help users understand threats and control how they respond. Fraud evolves constantly, and so do we. We work directly with users to understand emerging attacks, turn advances in ML and AI into effective defenses, and build products that protect and grow their revenue. What you’ll do As a software engineer on Radar, you’ll build products and infrastructure that help businesses understand and stop fraud and abuse. Your work will span backend services, enterprise APIs, and user experiences that put sophisticated prevention capabilities into our customers’ hands. You’ll own problems from investigation through launch, partnering with product managers, designers, and data scientists. You’ll have opportunities to scale systems that make real-time decisions across Stripe’s global payments network, bring advances in ML and AI into production, and build new products from scratch. Every improvement can have a direct impact on the revenue our users retain and the legitimate customers they serve. 4e3e7f0b2cac.title: Applied AI Engineer, Digital Natives
4e3e7f0b2cac.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works.

Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About the Role

As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale.

You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in Paris. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees

In this role, you will:

 - Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.

 - Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.

 - Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.

 - Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.

 - Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.

 - Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.

 - Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.

 - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, product engineering or technical consulting.

 - Are fluent in both French and English

 - Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or engineering of production systems—not only program or stakeholder management.

 - Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.

 - Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.

 - Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.

 - Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

 - Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.

 - Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.

 - Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. 

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. 9c18eaebf974.title: Product Manager - Data Platform
9c18eaebf974.description:
Spotify’s mission is to unlock the potential of human creativity by giving a million creative artists the opportunity to live off their art and billions of fans the chance to enjoy and be passionate about these creators.
Data is a means to an end, and Spotify extracts value from data through application. The Data Platform Studio helps Spotify win by enabling the application of data in an intuitive and efficient way.
Data Platform is responsible for how data is collected, processed, stored, governed, and made available to the thousands of engineers, data scientists, analysts, and machine learning practitioners who build Spotify’s products. As AI agents increasingly generate code, write data pipelines, and power personalized user experiences, Data Platform sits at the center of one of the most important infrastructure domains at Spotify.
We're looking for a passionate Product Manager to join the team responsible for Spotify’s data catalogue, metadata, and data lineage capabilities. In this role, you'll own the strategy and roadmap for a critical part of Spotify's data ecosystem, helping users discover, understand, trust, and safely use data at scale. You'll work closely with engineers, designers, data scientists, and product teams across Spotify to make working with data faster, safer, and more intuitive.

What You'll Do
Develop and own the product strategy and roadmap for Spotify's data catalogue, metadata, and data lineage domain. Diagnose and deeply understand the needs of Spotify's data community, including data engineers, data scientists, analysts, ML engineers, and increasingly AI agents. Identify and prioritize the highest-impact problems to solve, balancing user needs, business priorities, platform requirements, and regulatory considerations. Evaluate and deliver solutions through building, buying, or integrating third-party products and capabilities. Define success metrics and KPIs that measure adoption, value creation, and business impact. Build strong relationships with internal product, engineering, analytics, and data teams to understand workflows, gather feedback, and shape future platform investments. Collaborate closely with engineering, design, and data science partners to deliver high-quality platform experiences. Influence stakeholders across the Data Platform Studio and broader Spotify organization to align around product direction and priorities. Help shape how Spotify approaches metadata, governance, discoverability, lineage, and trust in an increasingly AI-driven world. Stay informed on industry trends across data platforms, developer tools, AI/ML infrastructure, analytics, and data governance.
Who You Are
You have 2+ years of Product Management experience, ideally working on platform products, developer tools, data infrastructure, analytics platforms, or data governance systems. You have a technical foundation through a degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, and/or prior experience in engineering or technical roles. You are comfortable working with engineers and can engage in technical discussions while representing customer and business needs. You are an excellent communicator and collaborator who can build alignment across teams with different priorities and levels of technical expertise. You have strong systems-thinking skills and can connect workflows, platforms, users, and business outcomes. You have empathy for people who work with data and understand the challenges they face every day. You enjoy working through ambiguity, breaking down complex problems, and creating clarity for teams. You are curious about how AI is transforming the data landscape and are excited to help shape that future. You lead with humility, build trust through collaboration, and help teams move forward with focus and momentum.
Where You'll Be
This role is based in London or Stockholm We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

69a236a05a68.description:
Mission Brief 

As LCA & Environmental Data Specialist, you will establish our Life Cycle Assessment and environmental data capabilities from the ground up. Your mission is to create a reliable environmental data foundation, conduct Life Cycle Assessments in accordance with recognized standards and translate complex environmental data into meaningful insights. You will work closely with Engineering, Procurement, Manufacturing, Testing, Infrastructure and other teams to understand the environmental impact of our product throughout its lifecycle.

 

Your Role in Our Space Mission: 

  • Life Cycle Assessment: Conduct and further develop Life Cycle Assessments (LCA) for our product, components, materials, and processes in accordance with ISO 14040 and ISO 14044. 
  • LCA Methodology & Modelling: Define goal and scope, develop Life Cycle Inventories, perform impact assessments, interpret results and document assumptions, limitations, and methodological choices. 
  • Environmental Data Collection: Collaborate closely with Engineering, Procurement, Manufacturing, Infrastructure and Testing to actively collect and understand the environmental, operational, material and supplier data required for LCA. 
  • Environmental Data Management: Establish structured and scalable processes for environmental data, ensuring data quality, consistency, completeness and traceability. 
  • LCA Tools & Databases: Develop and maintain LCA models, datasets and Life Cycle Inventories in openLCA and relevant LCA databases. 
  • Environmental Impact Analysis: Analyse LCA results, identify environmental hotspots and improvement opportunities and translate complex results into clear and actionable insights. 
  • Environmental Requirements & Performance: Support environmental and LCA-related customer, project, and contractual requirements and contribute to the development of environmental KPIs and methodologies to measure and track environmental performance. 
  • Ecodesign Collaboration: Communicate relevant LCA results and environmental hotspots to the Ecodesign Engineer and work closely together to identify and evaluate potential environmental improvements. 

 

Qualification Checklist 

 

  • Degree in a relevant technical, scientific, environmental, or data-related field, such as Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Sustainability, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science or a comparable discipline.

f420627fab77.description:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners  with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments.

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions.

WHY JOIN US

  • The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty.
  • You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms.
  • We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing.

About the Team

Minerva is STARK's command and control software — the brain that connects operators to autonomous systems across multiple domains in real time. The Minerva team is a small, senior software group based in Berlin and Munich, working directly with our systems and hardware teams to build mission-critical C2 capabilities deployed in active operational environments.
We move fast, ship real software, and operate under constraints most engineers never encounter — low-bandwidth networks, air-gapped devices, high-stakes decision loops. There is no room for abstraction for its own sake. Everything we build ends up in the hands of real operators in the field.

Your Mission

You will be developing cutting-edge Computer Vision solutions and algorithms for our autonomous vehicles, bringing these onto our hardware in real time.

Responsibilities

  • Coding!

  • Building in areas including Object Detection, Tracking and guidance, target re-identification

  • Working through software design, and architecture, all the way through to implementation

  • Integrating onto our hardware in real time

  • Stay current with emerging technologies and industry trends, recommending and implementing innovations to improve our products and processes

  • Dive deep into the details to identify, understand, and solve difficult technical problems

  • Constantly be challenging requirements to determine what adds value and what is not

Required Skills

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering or a related field

  • Minimum of + 7 years of experience working as Computer Vision generalist

  • Advanced use of Python and strong in C++

  • Robotics, autonomous driving or aerospace experience is a big plus

  • Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to troubleshoot and resolve issues

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team environment

  • Adaptability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic startup environment with a strong drive for innovation and continuous improvement

  • Ability to travel as needed

Nice-To-Have

 

If you're interested in building the future of European Defence with us, and you see yourself reflected on the description above, please send us your CV in English. We're looking forward to meeting you!

 

SECURITY CLEARANCE

Due to the nature of our work in the defence sector, candidates must be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate security clearance required for this position. Details will be provided during the recruitment process.

You will work in a high-density engineering environment alongside robotics, safety, and mission planning experts. If you care about RAII, memory safety, and squeezing every ounce of performance out of real hardware in the field to ensure mission success, this is the role.
What we build:

  • The System Brain: You will develop the core C++ services that orchestrate UAV and USV swarms, maintaining a synchronized and robust battlefield state across distributed systems.
  • Mission Control APIs: You will design and implement high-performance gRPC and REST APIs that bridge the gap between our frontend C2 interface and the autonomous vehicles in the field.
  • Real-Time Data Pipelines: You will build and optimize the telemetry pipelines that handle high-frequency data from diverse sensors, ensuring low-latency synchronization and delivery.
  • Scalable Architecture: You will expand our current C++ architecture to support "affordable mass"—scaling from controlling 4 to 20+ vehicles simultaneously.
  • Tactical Integration: You will implement military standards and protocols (such as STANAG), ensuring our systems are interoperable and battle-ready.
  • Robustness & Testing: You will build and maintain the test suites, ensuring our code performs reliably under the most contested conditions.

 

Responsibilities

 

  • A C++ Native: You write clean, performant Modern C++ (17/20/23). You understand the cost of every allocation and the value of a deterministic system.
  • Systems-Minded: You think in terms of data flows, state machines, and concurrency. You understand that in our domain, "late data is wrong data."
  • A Problem Solver: You dive deep into the details to identify, understand, and solve difficult technical problems at the hardware-software boundary.
  • High Agency

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions.

WHY JOIN US

  • The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty.
  • You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms.
  • We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing.

ABOUT THE TEAM

STARK is a European defence technology company building the next generation of unmanned systems. You will join our dynamic Flight Operations team dedicated to demonstrating, testing, and deploying high-performance autonomous platforms. In this role, you will bridge the gap between engineering development, flight testing, and high-visibility field operations across national and international settings.

Your mission is to fly our multirotor platforms flawlessly under real-world, high-visibility conditions, at home in Germany and internationally, showcasing product capabilities to internal stakeholders, partners, and customers.

  • Extensive flight experience and valid remote pilot certifications for UAV multirotor systems (e.g., A1/A3, A2, STS/SORA equivalents).

5390b0329b25.title: Software Engineer, Applied AI
5390b0329b25.description: About CircuitHub CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries. We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies. The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further. The Role CircuitHub makes electronics on demand. Engineers upload a circuit board design; we buy the parts, build the board in our own robotic factory and ship it. More and more of that business is now run by AI agents, and we want you to help build them. These aren't chatbots. Our agents have real jobs: They inspect boards. An agent checks camera images of every panel we build for wrong, rotated or missing parts. They program robots. Agents read datasheets so our pick-and-place machines know how to handle each new part. They watch the factory. They spot stray parts in robot storage, diagnose printer faults and clear stuck machines. They run the back office. They book supplier invoices, chase late orders, explain quotes and triage bugs. They write our code. Most of what our team ships starts in an agent session. What you'll do Find a process people still do by hand and automate it end to end: decide what needs judgement and what needs plain code, build the tools, and prove it works before it runs alone. Then make it cheaper, faster and right more often. You'll also improve the platform every agent runs on, and work closely with the people your work serves, from factory operators to finance. How we build Evals first. An agent earns the right to work alone: blind tests against people's verdicts, shadow runs beside the humans, replays of past decisions. We track accuracy and cost per run, and re-test whenever we change a model, a prompt or the effort level. Agents judge, code writes. Agents return structured answers. Plain code checks them against a second source and makes every change. Classical first, model second. Cheap vision and maths narrow the problem so the model only looks where it matters. Safe by construction. Agents work in sandboxed cloud machines that never hold real credentials, and tool calls are built so a business action can't run twice. Recent work Image alignment ranks the parts on each board photo. The worst 20% of parts hold about 90% of real defects, so the agent only inspects those. In a blind re-run it caught all 13 defects operators had marked. A photo check for stray parts in robot storage scored 10 out of 10 blind, at about 8¢ a photo. The model it replaced caught about half. Agent tool calls leave durable receipts, so a session killed mid-deploy resumes without sending the same email or order twice. Invoices extracted from supplier emails matched what a person had entered 66 times out of 66. A constraint solver replans the whole factory every two minutes, across robots, ovens and people. What we look for You've put LLM agents into production and can tell us what broke and how you knew it was working. You're a strong software engineer first. Most of this job is real engineering, not prompting: concurrency, idempotency, data modelling, security. You build the eval before you trust the result. You like the physical world: cameras, robots, parts rotated by 90°. Bonus: computer vision, optimisation or electronics. Stack Agents: Claude Code, Codex, Claude and OpenAI APIs, MCP, skills in plain Markdown Code: TypeScript (Bun, React), Python (FastAPI, Dagster, OpenCV, OR-Tools), PostgreSQL Infra: Nix and NixOS, Nomad, Terraform, Vault, AWS, Modal sandboxes, OpenTelemetry Pay UK £80k–£125k · US $125k–$250k, depending on experience, plus equity. Our team is focused on building a scalable, reliable, and high-quality internal tooling platform that supports Wolt, DoorDash, and Deliveroo's operations and business. The team plays an important role in improving how engineers build, test, and ship software across the organization, with a strong emphasis on reusable libraries, micro-frontend architecture, and agentic development: building the platform where AI agents can take changes from task to merged PR safely and reliably without lowering the quality bar. Currently, we are focused on unifying our frontend platforms, evolving shared components and library development, improving developer productivity, and enabling teams to deliver more independently through better architecture and tooling. It's an exciting time to join because the team has strong ownership and a broad technical impact. We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who can take ownership of complex technical initiatives across both frontend and sometimes backend and infra domains. In this role, you'll work primarily with TypeScript, React, Node.js, CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Buildkite), and MFE architecture to build scalable, maintainable solutions that support multiple product teams and business areas. Success in this role means becoming a trusted technical owner who consistently delivers reliable solutions and helps the team execute more effectively. Six months into the role, we'd expect you to be independently leading technical initiatives and contributing meaningfully to architecture and delivery planning. This role offers the opportunity to solve challenging engineering problems with visible impact across the business. It's especially exciting for someone who enjoys combining product engineering with platform thinking, improving developer workflows, and building systems that scale across teams and domains. AI Fluency: Work agent-first in your own day-to-day: delegate implementation to agents, and focus your judgment on direction, architecture, and verifying outcomes. 📍This role can be based in our Berlin tech hub. Track record of diagnosing and resolving complex performance, reliability, or DX issues in large frontend codebases. 45c5abbfceab.description:
Raisin is the world’s leading platform for savings and investment products. Founded in 2012, the FinTech connects consumers with banks in the EU, the UK and the US. This gives consumers better interest rates and banks a diversified form of refinancing. Our vision is to offer savings and investments without barriers and thus open up the global 160 trillion euro market.

Raisin currently employs more than 800 people from over 75 countries worldwide. Today, the platform holds over 80 billion euros in assets from more than one million investors which have accrued over 5 billion euros in returns.

Team

AI Enablement builds Raisin's internal AI platform. We make it easy and safe for every team, from engineering and product to business operations, to use AI in their daily work and in the products they build.

We provide the shared foundation for that: governed access to AI models and tools, the controls that keep data secure and usage auditable, and the visibility teams need to run AI reliably and cost-effectively. We also shape how Raisin builds software with AI, from AI-assisted coding to agentic workflows that support teams across the development lifecycle. Because Raisin operates in regulated financial services, security and compliance are core to how we design the platform.

The team is growing, and you will shape both what it builds and how it works.

Your Responsibilities

As Engineering Lead, you lead the engineers who build Raisin's internal AI platform and drive the company's AI-assisted engineering practices. You are accountable for the team's delivery, growth, and maintaining the AI platform users' trust. 

You stay close to the technology, because in a field that changes this quickly, good leadership decisions depend on understanding the technical details.

Lead and grow the team

  • Hire, onboard, and develop engineers, and build a team that works autonomously across platform engineering, infrastructure, and AI.
  • Hold regular 1:1s, set clear expectations, and agree individual development plans with each engineer.
  • Give timely feedback, recognise strong performance, and address low performance early.
  • Create an environment of trust, open communication, and continuous learning, so the team keeps up with a fast-moving field without burning out.

Own delivery and operations

  • Own end-to-end delivery, from planning and estimation through implementation and release, balancing new capabilities with reliability and maintenance.
  • Make sure the platform runs well in production: on-call, incident handling, and service levels for the systems other teams rely on.
  • Spot risks and blockers early and resolve them, or escalate in time with a clear proposal.
  • Turn the AI strategy into quarterly goals and a roadmap the team commits to, together with your manager and stakeholders.

Run the platform as a product

  • Work with engineering, product, and business stakeholders to understand their needs and decide what the platform should offer next.
  • Measure adoption, reliability, cost, and impact, and use that data in planning and when reporting to leadership.
  • Manage the cost of AI usage and tooling, including budgets, licences, vendor relationships, and build-versus-buy decisions.

Shape the technical direction

  • Work with the team's tech leads on architecture and key technical decisions, and stay hands-on in design discussions, reviews, and selected implementation work.
  • Work with security, legal, and compliance colleagues to keep the platform and the company's use of AI secure and compliant.
  • Help engineering teams across Raisin adopt AI in their work through documentation, workshops, and direct support.

Your Profile

What you bring

  • 3+ years leading engineers as an Engineering Manager, Engineering Lead, or Team Lead, including hiring and performance management.
  • 7+ years in software engineering overall, with a background in backend, platform, infrastructure, or developer tooling.
  • Experience leading a team that builds for internal customers, such as a platform, developer tooling, or shared services used by other engineers.
  • A track record of delivering production systems that other teams depend on, including ownership of their reliability.
  • A practical understanding of modern AI integration, such as LLM APIs, AI coding assistants, and agentic workflows, deep enough to evaluate technical decisions and challenge the team. You use AI tools in your own work.
  • Clear communication with engineers, product, and business stakeholders, and fluency in English.

Nice to have

  • Experience leading distributed or hybrid teams.

Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote position. We are looking for candidates in the UK, Ireland, Spain, Germany or Sweden.

Senior Software Engineer - Security Assurances

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Security Assurance to join our GRC engineering team. We are building a security system that’s automated at scale, rigorously data-driven, and built from the ground up with defense-in-depth and self-healing in mind. We support a highly autonomous, remote-first, cloud-native organization. We are a technical team that can build any tool we need, while knowing when to buy to improve velocity.

To support our growth and ambitious vision, we embrace agile principles and values, share openly, apply context-driven security mechanisms, default to action, and have an OSS-first mindset. We are a 100% remote company. We believe in high-velocity but sustainable expectations and timeframes, giving people the room to do great work.

The Opportunity:

You will work to build out our security observability, compliance, and control management systems and tools. You will develop services and tools to proactively defend our systems, provide visibility to our security state, and give engineers and stakeholders guardrails and paved roads to behave securely. You will collaborate across your team, the security department, and wider Grafana to write and deploy security policies across all of our SDLC, applications, and infrastructure.

This is a very technical, hands-on keyboard software engineering, so development experience is critical. You will ideally have some experience building, implementing and improving the maturity of security programs in Cloud-based SaaS organizations. Knowledge of security standards and frameworks (ISO, FedRAMP, PCI-DSS, GDPR, etc) is useful, but the disposition to quickly learn new things is more important than rote knowledge. You will work alongside other security engineers, full-stack developers, and customer-facing teams. Experience guiding and negotiating with peers, stakeholders, customers, and auditors is a plus. 

What You’ll Be Doing:

2247ca51e58b.title: Staff Engineer
2247ca51e58b.description: About Andercore Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry. Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell. We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought. We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded. Where we are today: Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth. About the role Andercore runs global trade end to end, from sourcing and pricing to sales, logistics and financing, and AI agents do a growing share of that work. Order values are high and prices and stock change daily, so the systems underneath have to be fast, correct and reliable at all times. As a Staff Engineer, you own our hardest technical problems and set the architecture across teams. You focus on what a fast-growing trading business cannot afford to get wrong: speed, reliability, security and observability. You report to our VP Engineering and work closely with our Senior Product Engineers, QA and product managers. You stay hands-on: you write code, review designs and raise the bar for everyone around you Tech stack Java 21 and Spring Boot 3, Python, LangGraph and LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini), PostgreSQL, Kinesis, AWS with Terraform, GitHub Actions, and TypeScript with Node.js, Next.js and React. Including Salesforce, which we are moving our transaction core out of. What you will do Set the technical direction across teams: define the target architecture, write the RFCs behind big decisions, and make sure teams build towards the same picture. Lead the hardest technical work yourself, from design to production, instead of only advising on it. Shape the carve-out of our transaction core from Salesforce into a modern, modular core system, with a migration path that never disrupts daily trading. Make reliability, security and observability part of how we build: monitoring, alerting, incident response and postmortems that lead to real changes. Design how our AI agents act safely on money-touching paths, with evaluations, guardrails, audit trails and human review where it matters. Set standards for correctness and data integrity, including idempotency, validation and testing, together with QA. Mentor engineers through design reviews, pairing and direct feedback, and help us hire by defining what great engineering looks like at Andercore. In your first six months, you might Design the architecture of our pricing engine so it scales with a growing assortment and more markets, and serves correct prices to sales, and later directly to customers, in milliseconds. Lay out the target architecture and first steps for moving our transaction core off Salesforce. Build the observability and incident setup that lets us catch problems before customers or colleagues notice them What you bring At least 8 years of experience building and running software in production, including systems where errors cost real money. A track record of setting architecture across several teams, through influence rather than a management title. Experience designing transactional, distributed and event-driven systems, with a strong focus on correctness, failure modes and performance. Hands-on depth in reliability, security and observability, and experience leading incidents and postmortems. Experience in a fast-growing company, and a track record of solving business problems, not only technical ones. AI is part of your daily work. Experience building or evaluating AI agents in production is a strong plus. Über uns QuantumDiamonds GmbH mit Hauptsitz in München entwickelt und fertigt Halbleiter-Inspektionssysteme auf Basis von Quantensensorik. Das 2022 aus der Technischen Universität München gegründete Unternehmen nutzt Stickstoff-Fehlstellen-Zentren (NV-Zentren) in Diamanten, um elektrische Ströme mit Mikrometer-Präzision innerhalb fortschrittlicher 2,5D- und 3D-Chiparchitekturen abzubilden. This is not a client-facing role. The problem: EvalOps How do we prove an AI system acts as expected under various conditions? We will explore EvalOps : the methods and tools used to check whether domain-specific AI systems meet their behavioral requirements. Among the key challenges for operating AI systems are nondeterminism, ground-truth curation, evaluation metric-design, latency and costs. EvalOps need to overcome all of them in a disciplined way. These questions will guide the initial work: Regression suites : How can domain experts turn traces, code, and prompts into useful evals in a way that scales? Coverage estimation : How can we quantify the gaps between an eval suite and the range of expected agent behaviors? Live monitoring : Is it possible to detect anomalous behaviour in production with a similar precision to regression evals? Eval analysis : How much evidence is enough to act (e.g., deploy, debug, roll back a feature, choose a different model)? You will help refine them, test approaches, create assets, and pose new questions. The role As an AI Builder, you will take an open EvalOps problem from investigation to a working prototype, ready to be tested. Whatever your focus, you will be expected to take a problem through to a useful result. Here is what that means in practice: Research emerging AI and evaluation capabilities and distinguish substance from hype. Understand the user, workflow, domain, and organisational problem around the work. Evaluate usefulness, quality, safety, and reliability with appropriate evidence. Communicate decisions and learning clearly. Create assets that other people can understand, use, and improve. Code and build end to end. This shared foundation leaves room for different strengths and interests. Each AI Builder will then develop greater depth in one of three pillars. Three pillars, different passions Pillar Driving question Possible EvalOps focus Product What should we build? Workflows and interfaces that help domain experts create evals, inspect traces, understand results, and make decisions. Engineering How should we build it? Dependable and scalable evaluation infrastructure, trace processing, monitoring, and governance tooling. Data Science How do we know it works? Coverage measures, sampling strategies, scoring methods, statistical tests, anomaly detection, and reasoning under uncertainty. We expect every AI Builder to develop a practical foundation across all three pillars and to pursue greater depth in the one that most strongly matches their passion. What we value Problem obsession . A difficult question captures your curiosity. You keep returning to it, pursue ideas without waiting for instructions, and care deeply about finding an answer that works. Initiative and follow-through . You turn uncertainty into something you can investigate, test, and improve—and stay resourceful when the first approach fails. Evidence of making things work . Show us something you created, the decisions you made, and what you learned along the way. Independent judgment . You test new capabilities yourself, distinguish evidence from enthusiasm, and change your mind when the findings warrant it. Generosity in collaboration . You explain your thinking, seek candid feedback, act on it, and help others make progress. What is required You are pursuing a Master’s degree. You can write code and turn an idea into working, tested software. You can work from Tübingen and communicate fluently in English, our company language. Relevant fields include Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Physics, Bioinformatics, Computational Neuroscience, Medical Informatics, Quantitative Data Science, Cognitive Science. Learn what works and what breaks in real enterprise AI systems, with access to problems from EggAI’s client work Meaningful ownership . The Internship Programme at Graphcore

Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence.

What you’ll work on

Use your programming skills and curiosity to help AI models run efficiently on next-generation Graphcore hardware. 

In AI Compute Libraries & Performance, you’ll contribute to C++ libraries and compute kernels for machine learning workloads. Your work will include: 

  • Developing compute kernels: Implement and improve operations such as matrix multiplication (GEMM), convolutions, reductions, elementwise operations and fused kernels that combine multiple operations. 
  • Understanding and improving performance: Use profiling and microbenchmarks to measure execution speed and investigate how threading, cache locality, memory layout and kernel launch efficiency affect performance. 
  • Checking correctness and reliability: Build regression tests and numerical checks, investigate issues and improve the quality of the libraries our customers use. 

Through these projects, you’ll develop practical experience connecting numerical computing with how code runs on hardware, helping deliver software that is fast, accurate and reliable. 

Your team and support

You’ll join a team building high-performance compute libraries that help customers get more from Graphcore hardware. Our work brings together machine learning, numerical computing and accelerator performance, with colleagues sharing their expertise to solve engineering problems.

You’ll contribute to clearly scoped projects and build your skills with guidance from engineers working in performance and low-level software. Together, we use profiling, experiments and technical reviews to compare approaches, understand trade-offs and improve our solutions. 

Your buddy will help you settle in, get familiar with our tools and ways of working, and find the right people to ask. Your manager will meet with you regularly to agree goals, offer feedback and discuss your development, including time for learning. 

We welcome different perspectives and make space for everyone to contribute. Questions, alternative approaches and requests for help are part of how we work. As you take on more responsibility, your colleagues will help you work through challenges, and your ideas will be listened to and discussed respectfully. 

How you’ll learn and grow

Over the 12 weeks, you’ll build performance engineering skills through hands-on work on compute kernels, benchmarks and tests. 

Profiling and experiments will help you understand where time is spent and how changes to code and data layout affect performance. Numerical validation and regression testing will show you how to check that an optimisation preserves correct results and continues to work as software changes. 

Working with specialists and discussing technical trade-offs will help you develop your engineering judgement, explain your findings and connect mathematical operations to efficient implementations on hardware.

What we're looking for

  • Currently studying towards a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Maths, Machine Learning, Data Science or a related field
  • Experience with C or C++11, plus familiarity with Python or scripting tools for automation and testing
  • An understanding of linear algebra, numerical methods or scientific computing
  • Problem-solving skills and collaborative approach to unfamiliar technical challenges

Previous industry experience is not required. Tell us what you built or investigated through coursework, personal or team projects or other relevant experience, how you approached it and what you learned.

Coursework or experience with machine learning frameworks, parallel programming, code optimisation, maths libraries or performance analysis would be useful. These are additional strengths, rather than essential requirements.
