e5b8b91b5598.title: 3D Computer Vision Research Engineer - World Map
e5b8b91b5598.description: About Niantic Spatial AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time. That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are. In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right. Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us. About the Role You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems. The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves. You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model. What You'll Do Geospatial Registration — Develop and advance algorithms for world-scale georeferencing and registration across imagery, 3D reconstructions, point clouds, and geographic reference data. 3D Geometry & Correspondence — Build and improve methods spanning multi-view geometry, SfM, SLAM, feature matching, learned correspondence, bundle adjustment, point-cloud registration, and ICP. Data & Evaluation — Create the data and evaluation flywheel for world-scale mapping — design and maintain large-scale datasets, pipelines, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies that expose hard failure modes, accelerate research iteration, and support production. Learning-Based 3D Reasoning — Explore and develop learning-based approaches for geospatial understanding, combining transformers and 3D foundation models with geometric priors and uncertainty modeling. Production Robustness — Design robust solutions for challenging real-world conditions: sparse or noisy GPS, changing appearance, inconsistent reconstruction quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps. Cross-Functional Collaboration — Partner with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping — as well as engineering and product teams — to identify high-impact problems and turn research breakthroughs into end-to-end production systems. Research Communication — Share results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, and internal presentations; contribute to publications and open research where appropriate. What You'll Bring Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Photogrammetry, or a closely related field — or equivalent research or industry experience. Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, machine learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related area. Demonstrated experience with 3D geometry and several relevant areas — multi-view reconstruction, SfM, SLAM, camera pose estimation, point-cloud registration, image-based localization, georeferencing, or sensor fusion. The ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose the right mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously. Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML and scientific-computing libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy). Strong software engineering skills — you can turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems. A track record of taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data. Clear written and verbal communication; able to collaborate effectively across research and engineering disciplines. Nice to Have PhD in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, photogrammetry, geodesy, remote sensing, or a related field — not required, but valued. A strong publication record or active involvement in the research community at venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, SIGGRAPH, 3DV, ICRA, or RSS. Experience with learning-based approaches for visual or 3D understanding — transformers, point transformers, foundation models, or methods combining learned representations with explicit geometric priors. Experience with aerial or satellite imagery, GNSS/GPS, geodesy, mapping systems, or large-scale spatial data. Evidence of technical leadership, mentorship, or successful cross-functional delivery. Compensation & Benefits Base salary: Competitive market rate. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. Location & Work Model This role is based in our London office, with three days per week in office. We welcome applications from candidates

0f201dd00b4d.description: About Us: At Upvest, we are on a mission to make investing as easy as spending money . Upvest empowers businesses to offer a wide range of investment products and the best experience in the field of capital market investment and retirement planning. Upvest’s Investment API is easy to integrate so that fintechs and financial institutions can save resources and fully focus on their core business. We are proud to partner with Europe’s leading Fintechs and financial institutions such as DKB, Revolut, N26 and Raisin. Founded in 2017 by Martin Kassing, Upvest now brings together over 270 talented professionals from more than 70 nationalities. Upvest is backed by €280M in total funding from world-class investors, including BlackRock, Tencent, Sapphire Ventures, and Bessemer Venture Partners, Earlybird, Notion Capital, and Motive . Our latest €105M funding round in March 2026 - led by Sapphire and Tencent - serves as a massive catalyst for our growth, allowing us to offer premier investment experience. About the role: In 2027, Upvest is launching the PEA (Plan d'Épargne en Actions) on the French market with several leading fintechs. Within the Settlements & Transfers team, you will work across the full post-trade chain of securities account and PEA transfers: from instruction processing to settlement at Euroclear France, including relations with account keepers, custodians and issuers. This internship offers direct exposure to French and European post-trade operations during a product launch, with real responsibilities from your first weeks. What you’ll do: Incoming and outgoing transfers: Handle securities account (CTO) and PEA transfers with banks and brokers in France and across Europe, from receipt of the request to settlement of securities and cash. Counterparty and client relations: Ensure smooth communication with counterparties (banks, brokers, custodians) and our clients, and drive the follow-up of requests and reminders. Controls and reconciliation: Check securities and cash positions, reconcile movements with our custodian and analyse breaks. Fails and exception management: Investigate unsettled or rejected instructions, identify the root cause and coordinate resolution with counterparties and internal teams. PEA tax continuity: Review and record PEA tax statements (bordereaux d'information) to ensure the plan's tax history is fully preserved. Registered shares: Process operations on French registered shares (conversions, de/registrations). Reporting and continuous improvement: actively monitor SLAs and KPIs, write operating procedures and identify automation opportunities. What you bring: Education: Master's degree (M1 or M2) in Finance, Banking, Economics or Law from a business school, engineering school or university; gap-year students and recent Master's graduates able to sign an internship agreement are welcome. Languages: You have native-level or bilingual proficiency in French (C2) and are comfortable working in English. Experience: A first experience in banking, back office, middle office or securities operations is a strong plus, as is knowledge of the PEA, post-trade or Euroclear France. Analytical mindset: Rigour, attention to detail and a taste for solving complex problems. Tools: You're confident with spreadsheets ; knowledge SQL/Python is a plus. How we Upvest in you: Impact-driven work: We’re building the infrastructure that will power the future of investing in Europe. It’s complex, ambitious, and meaningful. You’ll work with modern technologies and create something entirely new. No legacy systems, no limits. Team celebrations: Participate in company-wide events, such as UpFest, dinners, offsites and our Holiday party, to connect with colleagues and celebrate our achievements. Inclusion : We’re committed to a culture where everyone belongs and thrives. Our Employee Resources Groups foster inclusion and connection, like Upfem Black at Upvest, Up&Out, and UpVergent. e4cd92a5111d.description: About Us: DeepJudge is Switzerland’s leading AI and ICT scale-up, transforming how law firms and legal departments access and leverage their knowledge. Founded by former Google search engineers with PhDs in AI from ETH Zurich, and backed by top-tier Silicon Valley investors, we are building the intelligence layer that powers the legal industry. Every firm can license the same AI models, but no two firms share the same institutional knowledge. Decades of experience, work product, and precedent are often trapped across systems, underused and inaccessible. DeepJudge makes this expertise instantly available through world-class enterprise search and AI infrastructure, enabling firms to automate workflows, build knowledge-powered applications, and turn experience into a lasting advantage. Our technology is trusted by many of the world’s leading law firms, including Freshfields, Gunderson Dettmer, Holland & Knight, Arent Fox, and Cozen O’Connor. Headquartered in Switzerland with a growing team across North America, we are expanding rapidly and shaping the future of how professional knowledge is discovered and applied. At DeepJudge, we move fast, think rigorously, and care deeply about what we build. We combine cutting-edge research with close collaboration with our clients to deliver solutions that truly make an impact. If you want to be part of a team defining how AI transforms high-stakes knowledge work, this is the place to do it. About the role: As a Site Reliability Engineer at DeepJudge, you own the reliability of the systems that leading law firms depend on every day. We run our AI search platform in dedicated production environments, each a large-scale search and retrieval system operating at very high data volumes, alongside our ingestion pipelines and data stores, on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds. Keeping those environments fast, available, and trustworthy is a genuine engineering challenge, and it's your mission. This is a technical, infrastructure-focused role: you'll spend your time in systems, code, and telemetry. You'll harden the platform so that classes of failure can't recur, build observability and SLOs to let us see problems before they surface, plan capacity ahead of relentless data growth, and automate away the toil of safely operating many production environments. You'll work across our deployment and infrastructure-as-code and partner closely with product engineering to feed reliability learnings back into the platform. If you like operating serious distributed systems at scale and turning firefighting into engineered reliability, this role is for you. Your responsibilities will include: Owning the availability, latency and performance of our production environments: large-scale search and retrieval services, ingestion and data stores on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds Owning the cloud infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds, networking, identity and access, compute and storage, and managing cloud capacity, quotas and cost as the fleet grows Improving deployment and infrastructure through code: GitOps-based configuration and deployment and infrastructure-as-code across our public and private clouds, with safe, previewed, recoverable production changes Defining and instrumenting SLOs and error budgets and building the dashboards, metrics and alerting that make production observable and actionable Reducing operational toil through automation and internal tooling written in Python and / or Go Provisioning and standardizing new production environments to a defined reliability bar You're a great fit if you: Have 3+ years in SRE, production / platform engineering, or infrastructure-heavy software engineering, operating real production systems under reliability expectations Are strong at container-orchestration operations in production and comfortable on at least one major public cloud Have solid cloud infrastructure experience on a major public cloud and a working grasp of cloud capacity, quotas, and cost Practice observability hands-on with metrics, logs and traces, and use it to root-cause live incidents Work fluently with infrastructure-as-code and GitOps Can code in Python and / or Go for automation, tooling, and reading and patching service code. Bring sound production judgment and document your work clearly for other engineers Bonus: experience operating a large-scale search or distributed data system, database operations, dedicated / enterprise-deployed software, or AI / enterprise-search infrastructure in regulated domains What you can look forward to: Owning the reliability of systems that the world's leading law firms rely on: real scale, real impact Deep, hands-on work with modern infrastructure: distributed search at very large scale, container orchestration across multiple clouds, and a mature infrastructure-as-code and GitOps stack A rigorous, high-urgency engineering culture founded by ex-Google search engineers and ETH Zurich AI PhDs The chance to build the reliability discipline, SLOs, incident practice, automation, from a strong foundation, not inherit a rigid one A collaborative team in Zurich shaping how AI transforms professional knowledge work At DeepJudge, we believe great teams are built on diverse perspectives and experiences. efd23dc20813.title: Software Engineer, Lab Automation
efd23dc20813.description: Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today. Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development. We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation. About the Role You'll build work-cell orchestration, instrument drivers, protocol scheduling, error-recovery logic, and monitoring. Physical systems fail in ways pure software doesn't — a plate gets stuck, a liquid handler skips a well, a temperature controller drifts. Your job is to make the system handle all of it gracefully. This is a broad, hands-on role for a strong engineer who wants their code to drive real machines and see it run the same day. About the Role Our lab produces binding data faster than any one person can look at it. Runs come off the Gators and the Carterra, go through our processing pipeline, and land in a review queue. Somebody with real judgment then has to decide: is this curve real? Is that a fit artifact or a genuine two-state binding event? Does this replicate get delivered, or does the sample get re-run? That person is you. The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams. This is a role for a scientist who is very good at kinetics and also likes people. If you like one but not the other, you'll be unhappy here. What You'll Do Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run. Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why. Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it. Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next. Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity. Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve. Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team. Work closely with production (what actually happened in the lab), QC (systematic quality), and customer success (the relationship around the science). What We're Looking For MSc / PhD in biochemistry, biophysics, or a relevant field, plus 3+ years working hands-on with binding kinetics. Deep SPR and BLI experience. Biacore, Carterra, Octet, Gator: the platform matters less than the fact that you've run these assays, troubleshot them, and interpreted a lot of data from them. You've seen enough sensorgrams to know immediately when one is lying to you. Real fitting judgment. 1:1 vs. bivalent, when steady-state is appropriate and when it isn't, how mass transport and avidity distort a result. You can defend a Kd, or refuse to report one. Strong data analysis skills. Python or R, enough to pull a few hundred results out of a database, fit them, plot them, and find the outliers. This role generates too much data to review by hand. You use AI tools seriously. We run on Claude Code and similar tooling internally, and the people who get the most done here are the ones who reach for it by default: writing the analysis script, querying the database, building the one-off dashboard. You don't need to have done this before, but you need to want to. If your instinct is that real scientists do it by hand, this isn't the place. A self-starter who works independently. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue every morning. You'll figure out what matters most, go do it, and tell us what you found. A fast learner. About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  

What to Expect

We are seeking a Senior Cryogenic Engineer to support and develop advanced cryogenic platforms for our SNSPD (Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detector) product line, with a strong emphasis on next-generation rack-mountable systems.

You will join a cross-functional team dedicated to advancing world-class quantum technologies that address some of the most complex challenges in computing, networking, and sensing. In this role, you will play a central part in the development lifecycle, overseeing cryogenic subsystems and ensuring robust, reliable 2K cryo-systems that can be deployed across internal and customer environments, while remaining maintainable and adaptable as the technology evolves.

What You'll be Doing

Working at the intersection of engineering and innovation, you will lead system-level specification, integration, and testing of cryogenic platforms tailored to SNSPD requirements. You will collaborate closely with internal teams, subcontractors, and external partners to design, configure, and improve deployable systems, while also providing operational support for existing platforms.

What you'll Bring

This position suits a highly experienced engineer with a strong background in cryogenic systems, hands-on expertise with cryostats and related technologies, and the ability to drive integration efforts across multidisciplinary teams and external vendors.

You'll be a great fit with:

  • Master’s degree (PhD preferred) in applied physics, system engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field, with 5-7+ years of experience in the cryogenic industry
  • Proven experience designing, evaluating, and maintaining complex cryogenic systems, including dilution, sorption, and 1 K cryostats
  • Strong knowledge of cryogenic wiring, sensors, electronics, and CAD-based design and manufacturing processes
  • Experience collaborating with cryogenic vendors, subcontractors, and external design partners on system integration
  • Desirable expertise in fibre or free-space optics, superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors, and leading integration projects

d57f11bef8c6.title: PLC Software Engineer - The Netherlands
d57f11bef8c6.description: Ready to build the software behind real-world renewable energy installations? At Bright Renewables, your PLC software doesn’t stay behind a desk. You’ll see it come to life in complex industrial installations for renewable gas and CO₂ technologies. As a PLC Software Engineer , you’ll be involved in the complete automation lifecycle - from software design and programming to testing, commissioning, troubleshooting, and optimization. You’ll have the opportunity to contribute to technical decisions, help shape our automation standards, and work alongside experienced colleagues as part of an international software engineering team of around 10 engineers. Together, you’ll collaborate across the Netherlands, Latvia, and Poland to develop and deliver reliable, innovative automation solutions. Why this role? You’ll get the opportunity to: Own your solutions - contribute to software solutions throughout the project lifecycle, from design and programming to testing and commissioning; Work on real installations - solve automation challenges in complex renewable energy plants; Have technical influence - contribute to software standards, templates, concepts, and ways of working, within a team that values collaboration and embraces innovative ideas from everyone; Keep developing - work alongside experienced Electrical and Software Engineers and continue building your technical expertise; Work internationally - collaborate with colleagues and project teams in the Netherlands, Poland, Latvia and beyond, including regular international travel to visit our offices and project sites; Choose what works for you - work 32 or 40 hours per week, with flexible starting times and opportunities to work from home; Make an impact - use your automation expertise in technologies that contribute directly to the energy transition. What will you do? As a PLC Software Engineer, you design, develop, test, and commission PLC and SCADA control systems for technologies such as gas upgrading and CO₂ liquefaction. You report directly to the Manager E&I and Software and work closely with Electrical Engineers, Process Engineers and fellow Software Engineers . Depending on your experience, you’ll also have the opportunity to take more technical ownership, contribute to software concepts and standards, and support colleagues with complex automation challenges. Your responsibilities include: Designing, programming, testing, and commissioning PLC and SCADA systems ; Developing control software for gas upgrading, CO₂ liquefaction, and other renewable energy technologies; Taking ownership of your software from engineering through commissioning; Testing and troubleshooting software during commissioning and operation; Analyzing and resolving software and control-related issues in existing installations; Implementing software updates and optimizations; Supporting Service Engineers with more complex automation and software questions; Contributing to software standards, templates, and automation concepts; Working closely with Electrical Engineers, Software Engineers, and other technical disciplines; Sharing knowledge and supporting colleagues within the engineering team. What do you bring? We’re looking for someone who enjoys solving technical challenges and wants to take responsibility for their own engineering work. Ideally, you have: A completed technical education in automation, mechatronics, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field; Several years of experience in PLC/SCADA engineering within an industrial environment; Hands-on experience in PLC programming, ideally with Siemens S7 and TIA Portal, combined with knowledge of WinCC SCADA, industrial communication networks, and remote access solutions. Experience with commissioning and troubleshooting industrial installations; A good understanding of automation architectures and industrial control systems; Good command of English, both spoken and written; Knowledge of OT security is a plus. What’s in it for you? We want to give you the technical freedom and working environment to do your best engineering work. You can expect: A competitive salary based on your experience and technical background; The option to work 32 or 40 hours per week; Flexible starting times between 7:00 and 9:00 a.m. ; Ample opportunities to work from home, including a one-time €250 allowance to set up your home office; An attractive annual profit-sharing scheme for employees with at least 12 months of service; An excellent pension scheme; 8% annual holiday allowance; A commuting allowance of €0.23 per kilometer, in accordance with our employment conditions; A high level of autonomy and responsibility; Plenty of opportunities for technical and professional development; An international engineering environment with both experienced professionals and engineers earlier in their careers; The opportunity to work with renewable energy technologies and contribute directly to the energy transition; A bike lease program and rewards for cycling to work; A modern, sustainably built working environment in Hengelo. About Bright Renewables Bright Renewables develops and delivers technologies for renewable gas and CO₂ capture, providing solutions from engineering and realization through to service and maintenance. Our installations convert biogas into renewable natural gas and capture, purify, and liquefy CO₂ for industrial reuse. We are part of HoSt Group , a family-owned Dutch company operating internationally in renewable energy technology. For you, that means working on international projects with the opportunities of a global organization, while keeping the short communication lines, technical freedom, and personal approach of a family-owned company. Interested? We’d like to get to know you. Apply by submitting your CV and motivation through the application button. Within 14 days, we’ll let you know whether we’d like to invite you for an interview. Would you first like to know more about the technology, team

2eee2988a6a2.title: AI Engineer
2eee2988a6a2.description: Who are we? Gain is the Private Markets Super App, a connected global platform transforming how leading investors, advisors, and corporates source, evaluate, and execute deals. By combining investment-grade intelligence, AI-powered workflows, and proprietary data in one unified platform, Gain enables top deal teams to move faster, reduce risk, and build conviction with confidence. Gain is trusted across more than $1 trillion of private capital, used by 100% of MBB and Big Four firms, and by 80% of the world’s top 20 M&A advisory houses. Recognized for fast innovation and impact, Gain has been named both US and EU Data Provider of the Year by PE Wire, awarded Global Financial Market Review’s Best Use of AI in Finance, and ranked in Sifted’s Top 100 Fastest-Growing Companies, the Forbes 1000, and the Deloitte Technology Fast 50. Gain operates globally with offices in New York, London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Warsaw, and Bangalore. How we work Predicting what isn't published. Many private companies publish little or no financial detail. Across a database of more than 5 million companies, we predict revenue and EBITDA from sparse labels, and we predict whether and when a company will be bought or sold, which is a time-to-event problem with censored data. Agents on a messy web. Our agents search, navigate and extract company data points from sources that contradict each other, then decide which source to trust before committing to an answer. Quality that holds while everything underneath moves. We're provider-agnostic. Model choices follow the evals, and we switch LLMs when the numbers say so. That only works if the evals are trusted. What will you do? The work is roughly half LLM agents and half custom ML, leaning slightly toward agents. The design of our agent pipelines: architecture, tools, and which model for which task. You'll shape the technical direction with our AI Lead. The evaluation behind agents and models: offline reference sets, live production evals, and the call on whether an improvement is real. Our prediction models for financials and deals: features, validation, retraining, and knowing when a simpler model wins. Getting work into production: trace where pipelines fail and fix the weakest links first, with compute, memory and model cost in view. Raising the bar in the team through design reviews, pairing, and an eval-first habit that sticks. In your first six months you'll own the evals for our agent pipelines, propose where we invest next, and ship measurable improvements to both the agents and the prediction models. Who are you? You've built and owned ML systems in production for years, typically 6+ in ML or software engineering. In the last 1–2 years you've shipped LLM agents or pipelines that real users depend on, not demos. You have modelling judgement. You've dealt with leakage, distribution shift and calibration on real data. You measure before you claim. You can build an evaluation set and tell an honest improvement from a lucky one. You care about the user outcome more than the technique. Ideas without a clear customer benefit don't get built here, however interesting. Nice to have: time-to-event modelling, noisy or conflicting data sources, financial or private-company data. No finance background needed. The team You'll join our Data & AI team of six and report to Renan, our AI Lead who's been building production models for >10 years. Our engineering team runs the infrastructure, and you shape what runs on it. The stack Core: Python (async, fully typed with Pydantic) and FastAPI LLMs: multiple providers behind our own provider-agnostic layer, with Pydantic AI for typed agents. Evals and observability: Pydantic Evals and Logfire Data: PostgreSQL with pgvector Cloud: GCP (Cloud Run, Cloud Tasks), Docker, GitHub Actions What do we offer? Competitive base salary and annual bonus linked to your performance / OKRs Attractive benefits including health & wellbeing allowance, work-from-home budget, learning & coaching benefits, etc. Flexible hybrid working model with 3 days per week in our Amsterdam office Healthy work-life balance allowing for planability and personal commitments Chance to grow with the company gaining increasing responsibilities, supported by lots of coaching and a feedback-driven approach Tremendous learning and career progression opportunities International environment with hubs in New York, London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Warsaw, and Bangalore Culture of trust, ownership and standard of excellence and a fun working atmosphere with regular outings and events Post product-market fit and aspiring unicorn status - this is an excellent time to join & grow with us! Does this sound like a perfect match? We are proud of our wonderful product and believe it has lots of potential. We are growing fast and having fun while building our platform and company. Does this sound like a team you would like to become a part of? Click ‘Apply’ and submit your CV, we are excited to get to know you and show you what we do! 1a211f194f4e.title: Data Analist
1a211f194f4e.description: Zie jij snel welke data nodig is om een businessvraag te beantwoorden? Als Data Analist binnen het Data & AI Office analyseer je data, vertaal je vraagstukken uit de business naar concrete inzichten en help je collega’s om die inzichten te gebruiken voor betere beslissingen. Ook onderzoek je waar AI waarde kan toevoegen en werk je mee aan praktische toepassingen die de manier van werken verbeteren. Je bent de schakel tussen de business en de specialisten binnen Data & AI. Daarmee zorg je ervoor dat goede ideeën niet blijven hangen in analyses of experimenten, maar leiden tot oplossingen die medewerkers daadwerkelijk gebruiken en die waarde opleveren voor onze leden. Wie ben jij Jij bent analytisch sterk en oprecht nieuwsgierig naar wat er binnen de business speelt. Je neemt geen genoegen met de eerste vraag, maar onderzoekt welk probleem er werkelijk moet worden opgelost en welke informatie nodig is om een goede beslissing te nemen. Je kunt schakelen tussen verschillende werelden. Je begrijpt de taal van de business, werkt zelf ook graag met data en kan goed samenwerken met technische dataspecialisten. Je hoeft niet zelf ieder model of datapipeline te bouwen, maar je begrijpt voldoende van data en AI om mogelijkheden te herkennen, inhoudelijke vragen te stellen en resultaten kritisch te beoordelen. Je communiceert helder en overtuigend. Je kunt complexe analyses eenvoudig uitleggen en helpt collega’s om inzichten en AI-oplossingen op een goede manier toe te passen. Daarbij ben je organisatiesensitief, verbindend en resultaatgericht. Je neemt eigenaarschap en blijft betrokken totdat een oplossing daadwerkelijk wordt gebruikt en waarde toevoegt. Wat neem je mee? hbo- of wo-werk- en denkniveau, bij voorkeur met een opleiding in Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Econometrie, Bedrijfskunde, Informatiekunde of een vergelijkbare richting; meerdere jaren relevante ervaring als data-analist, businessanalist of in een vergelijkbare rol; ervaring met het vertalen van businessvragen naar analyses, informatieproducten of datatoepassingen; goede kennis van data-analyse en ervaring met SQL en Snowflake; het vermogen om analyses te vertalen naar duidelijke adviezen en concrete verbeteracties; affiniteit met artificial intelligence en de nieuwsgierigheid om nieuwe toepassingen snel eigen te maken; ervaring met het begeleiden van stakeholders en stimuleren van adoptie; oog voor datakwaliteit, privacy en verantwoord gebruik van data en AI; sterke communicatieve en samenwerkingsvaardigheden; uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse taal, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. Wat ga je doen Je werkt vanuit het Data & AI Office binnen één of meerdere waardestromen van Univé. Je kent de doelstellingen, processen en uitdagingen van de waardestroom en onderzoekt samen met collega’s waar data en AI kunnen bijdragen aan betere dienstverlening, efficiëntere processen en onderbouwde besluitvorming. Je helpt de business om de juiste vragen te stellen. Je brengt informatiebehoeften in kaart, analyseert beschikbare data en vertaalt uitkomsten naar heldere inzichten en concrete aanbevelingen. Je onderzoekt ook waar voorspellende modellen, generatieve AI of andere slimme toepassingen medewerkers kunnen ondersteunen in hun dagelijkse werk. Je werkt intensief samen met collega’s uit de business, Business Informatie Analisten, data scientists, data engineers en andere specialisten binnen het Data & AI Office. Je verbindt de inhoudelijke kennis van de waardestroom met de mogelijkheden van data en AI. Tijdens de ontwikkeling bewaak je het doel en de toegevoegde waarde. Na oplevering help je de business om de oplossing te begrijpen, te gebruiken en verder te verbeteren. Concreet houd je je bezig met: ophalen en doorgronden van businessvragen binnen de waardestroom; herkennen en concretiseren van kansen voor data, analytics en AI; analyseren van data met SQL in Snowflake en Python en vertalen van de uitkomsten naar begrijpelijke inzichten en adviezen; ontwikkelen en verbeteren van rapportages, dashboards en andere informatieproducten; samen met data scientists en data engineers werken aan dataproducten en AI-toepassingen; formuleren van heldere requirements, use cases en acceptatiecriteria; ondersteunen van medewerkers en leidinggevenden bij het begrijpen en toepassen van data en AI; stimuleren van adoptie en datagedreven werken binnen de waardestroom; bewaken of een oplossing daadwerkelijk bijdraagt aan het oorspronkelijke businessdoel; signaleren van problemen rondom datakwaliteit, definities en beschikbaarheid; verantwoord omgaan met data en AI, met aandacht voor privacy, uitlegbaarheid en menselijke controle; delen van kennis, voorbeelden en succesvolle toepassingen binnen Univé. Je standplaats is Zwolle, maar we werken ook een dag in Assen. We werken hybride, waarbij je gemiddeld de helft van de tijd op kantoor werkt. Wat bieden wij Binnen het Data & AI Office krijg je een veelzijdige functie waarin je direct samenwerkt met de business en zichtbaar bijdraagt aan de ontwikkeling van Univé. Je krijgt de ruimte om kansen te signaleren, collega’s mee te nemen en ideeën om te zetten in toepassingen die in de praktijk waarde opleveren. Salaris en arbeidsvoorwaarden: deze functie is ingedeeld in schaal 9. Het jaarsalaris ligt tussen € 58.352 tot € 82.378 op basis van een 38-urige werkweek, inclusief vakantiegeld en dertiende maand en exclusief variabele beloning; Uitdagende projecten: je werkt aan organisatiebrede afwisselende vraagstukken op het snijvlak van data, AI, technologie en business; Ontwikkeling: we investeren in jouw persoonlijke en professionele groei met opleidingen, kennisdeling en ruimte om je verder te specialiseren; Ruimte voor initiatief: je krijgt de vrijheid om kansen te onderzoeken, voorstellen te doen en verbeteringen in gang te zetten; Moderne werkomgeving: je werkt met SQL in Snowflake. 708c1135b526.description: WAT GA JE DOEN? Account Business Reviews (ABR’s) vormen de rode draad in de gesprekken tussen onze accountmanagers en klanten. Tijdens deze periodieke meetings staan de samenwerking, prestaties, aandachtspunten, kansen en gezamenlijke vervolgstappen centraal. De voorbereiding kost nu veel tijd, omdat relevante informatie uit verschillende systemen en bronnen handmatig moet worden verzameld en samengevoegd. Jouw uitdaging is om te onderzoeken hoe informatie uit verschillende systemen binnen een veilige en gecontroleerde omgeving automatisch kan worden samengebracht en verwerkt tot een professioneel ABR-rapport. AI helpt bij het structureren, samenvatten en formuleren van relevante inzichten, aanbevelingen en onderwerpen voor het komende gesprek. ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Inference team brings OpenAI’s most capable research and technology to the world through our products. We empower consumers, enterprises and developers alike to use and access our state-of-the-art AI models, allowing them to do things that they’ve never been able to before. We focus on performant and efficient model inference, as well as accelerating research progression via model inference.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an engineer to lead the optimization of OpenAI’s state-of-the-art frontier models on TPUs. You will own performance across the full forward pass, from model code through kernels to execution on the hardware.

You’ll have broad technical ownership: identifying performance bottlenecks, choosing the most impactful improvements, and carrying them through implementation and validation. We welcome experience gained through either training or inference, with a strong foundation in optimizing real workloads on TPUs.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Optimize model execution on TPUs, improving performance across the complete forward pass and the interactions between model code, kernels, and hardware.

 - Profile workloads, identify bottlenecks, and implement improvements to latency, throughput, and hardware utilization.

 - Develop and optimize kernels, using an understanding of the surrounding model to guide implementation choices.

 - Explore techniques such as quantization to improve inference efficiency while preserving model quality.

 - Build benchmarks and tools to measure performance, validate correctness, and guide optimization work.

 - Partner with researchers and engineers to support new model architectures and bring performance improvements into production.
   


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have practical experience optimizing machine learning workloads on TPUs, through training, inference, or both.

 - Understand modern model architectures and how their computation maps onto accelerator hardware.

 - Can connect detailed kernel behavior to the performance of a complete model and work across these layers of the stack.

 - Bring strong software engineering skills and a systematic approach to profiling, debugging, and validating performance improvements.

 - Take ownership of open-ended technical problems and can identify priorities, make design decisions, and deliver working solutions.

 - Enjoys collaborating with researchers and engineers, learning unfamiliar parts of a system, and communicating technical tradeoffs.

 - Have experience with quantization or attention kernels, which would be especially useful in this role.

About the role

We’re looking for a product data scientist to help OpenAI create more value and drive sustainable growth for young people, families, and learners. You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly.

You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value.

You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety.

In this role, you will:

 - Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort.

 - Define what value and success mean. Develop an audience-specific measurement framework spanning activation, task success, learning progress, satisfaction, and durable retention. Connect these measures to product goals and assess whether repeat use reflects meaningful benefit.

 - Understand users and growth drivers. Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to uncover where people find value, where they struggle, and what helps them return. Combine behavioral data with surveys and user research to explain differences across ages, family roles, and learning contexts.

 - Measure what changes actually cause. Design experiments and holdouts to evaluate product and model changes. Apply causal methods when randomization is impractical, make assumptions explicit, and account for seasonality, audience composition, and effects that differ across segments.

 - Create alignment across teams. Bring a coherent view of audience value to work spanning multiple roadmaps. Help partners agree on priorities, success criteria, and the next questions to resolve, even when ownership is distributed and evidence is incomplete.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - A record of influencing product strategy and improving user outcomes through hands-on data science, including work from an ambiguous question to a decision and measurable impact.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills, sound statistical judgment, and practical experience with experiments, causal inference, cohort analysis, and measurement design.

 - The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement.

 - Clear communication and strong product judgment. You can make a recommendation, explain its limits, and influence collaborators across functions without relying on formal authority.

d18a98c4c5cd.title: Software Engineer, Enterprise Knowledge Platform
d18a98c4c5cd.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

The Enterprise Knowledge Platform team builds the data and action layer that connects Perplexity's agents to the systems where enterprise work happens. Useful agents need more than access to APIs: they need to discover the right tools, understand an organization's data and terminology, and act reliably within its permissions. This team brings native connectors, MCP servers, and CLI-backed tools into a consistent platform, and builds the marketplace through which customers adopt integrations and partners extend the ecosystem.



This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from designing connector infrastructure and semantic models to shipping the experiences customers use to discover, connect, and activate integrations. You'll build the runtime that executes tool calls, the knowledge layer that makes enterprise context reusable across connectors, and the developer and marketplace foundations that help the ecosystem grow. Working with AI Research and Enterprise teams, you'll turn fragmented systems into reliable, permission-aware capabilities that agents can use to complete real work. The impact is direct: every improvement helps customers put their existing software and knowledge to work through Perplexity.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the connector runtime that registers, hosts, and executes native connectors, hosted MCP servers, and CLI-backed tools through a consistent agent-facing interface.

 - Build the semantic and knowledge layer, including tool and entity schemas, capability metadata, relationships, organization-specific terminology, and reusable corrections, while preserving provenance and source-system permissions.

 - Design discovery, search, and recommendation systems that help agents find relevant tools and context and help users and organizations choose integrations that fit their work.

 - Build the marketplace and activation experience end to end, from browsing and recommendations to installation, configuration, admin enablement, and ongoing adoption.

 - Make connector execution reliable and observable, with structured results, retries, idempotency, pagination, rate-limit handling, and recovery from partial failures. Own reliability targets, production monitoring, and incident response.

 - Implement connector authentication, credential isolation, and permission enforcement, partnering with Trust & Governance, Security, and Backend Platform on shared policies and tenant boundaries.

 - Build the onboarding and publishing path for internal teams and external partners, including schemas, test fixtures, validation, review, and versioning.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.

 - Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable platforms that integrate heterogeneous APIs and services with clear security and isolation boundaries.

 - Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS and Kubernetes.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of the following:
   
   - Connector runtimes, API platforms, or MCP servers, including authentication and authorization.
   
   - Schema design, semantic modeling, or knowledge systems that capture relationships and organizational context.
   
   - Search, ranking, recommendation, or tool discovery systems.
   
   - Marketplaces, developer platforms, or enterprise onboarding and activation experiences.

cee1f37b4595.title: Principal Product Manager - Core Experience Platform
cee1f37b4595.description:
We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.
The Core Experience team builds the foundations that make Spotify feel connected, intuitive, and consistent wherever people listen. From Playlists to shared product capabilities, we help teams across Spotify create experiences that millions of listeners use every day.
We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to shape the future of these platforms. You'll set product direction, bring teams together around shared priorities, and help create the capabilities that make great listening experiences possible at scale. This is an opportunity to influence how Spotify's products evolve while making a meaningful impact on listeners and creators around the world.

What You’ll Do
Partner with engineering leaders to explore technical solutions, evaluate trade-offs, and guide decisions that improve product performance, reliability, and scalability. Develop shared platform capabilities that help teams build consistent, high-quality experiences across Spotify. Improve the adoption and long-term value of platform capabilities by gathering feedback, measuring outcomes, and supporting teams that use them. Balance new product opportunities with technical improvements, including system performance, quality, simplification, and platform migrations. Use experimentation, prototypes, technical exploration, and feedback to test ideas, learn quickly, and adapt your approach. Build alignment across teams by communicating priorities, dependencies, and trade-offs clearly, helping partners work toward shared outcomes.
Who You Are
You have 5+ years of product management experience, including experience building or improving technical platforms, shared systems, or capabilities that support consumer products. You understand client and backend technologies and can work with engineers to connect technical decisions to user needs and business outcomes. You're familiar with mobile development for iOS or Android, including areas such as app performance, reliability, user interface architecture, or design systems. You have experience guiding products or platforms beyond launch, improving adoption, managing technical debt, and supporting systems as needs evolve. You can evaluate technical trade-offs and make thoughtful decisions about when to improve existing systems, simplify solutions, or invest in new capabilities. You use data, research, experimentation, and sound judgment to make product decisions, including when traditional A/B testing isn't the right approach. You communicate complex ideas clearly, welcome different perspectives, and build strong relationships across engineering, design, and data teams. You're comfortable navigating ambiguity, taking ownership of complex challenges, and adapting your approach as you learn.
Where You’ll Be
This role is based in Stockholm or London. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.
Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.
 
At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

ef823bc5c3da.title: Business Development Representative (m/w/d) - AI Agent Platform
ef823bc5c3da.description: Ninox ist eine Berliner Low-Code-Plattform, mit der Teams genau die Geschäftsanwendungen bauen, die sie brauchen. Rund 80 Mitarbeitende, tausende Kundinnen und Kunden in ganz Europa, vom kleinen Team bis zum Großunternehmen. Ein Produkt, an dem Menschen wirklich hängen. Wir sind seit 12 Jahren am Markt, etabliert, wachsen und sind solide mit Wagniskapital finanziert. Worum es geht Du machst Outbound. Zu 100 %, und vor allem am Telefon. Du bekommst Zielaccounts aus Branchen, die wir vorab festlegen, findest dort die Menschen, die das Problem tatsächlich haben, rufst sie an — und buchst qualifizierte Erstgespräche für unsere Account Executives. Nach dem Handover übernimmt der AE. Dein Ergebnis ist das stattgefundene, qualifizierte Gespräch, nicht der Abschluss und nicht der Kalendereintrag. Der größte Teil unseres Geschäfts sind kleine und mittlere Unternehmen, dazu kommt ein solider Anteil Mid-Market. Innerhalb der Verticals, die für uns nachweislich funktionieren, gehen wir gelegentlich auch in größere Organisationen. Damit es keine Missverständnisse gibt: „Enterprise" heißt bei uns Unternehmen mit einigen hundert bis wenigen tausend Mitarbeitenden — nicht DAX-Konzern mit zweijährigem Beschaffungsprozess und Rahmenvertragsverhandlung. Du arbeitest auf Deutsch und auf Englisch, jeden Tag. Deutschland und Großbritannien sind unsere Kernmärkte, weitere europäische Länder kommen situativ dazu. Dein Umfeld, ehrlich beschrieben: Unser Vertrieb arbeitet heute Full-Funnel. Die Account Executives machen neben allem anderen rund eine Stunde Outbound pro Tag. Dazu kommt eine Kollegin bzw. ein Kollege mit ebenfalls reinem Outbound-Fokus, allerdings auf Kooperationen, Webinare und Partner. Du bist damit die erste Person bei uns, die ausschließlich und direkt auf Neukunden-Erstgespräche geht. Das heißt: Es gibt Erfahrung im Haus, an die du andocken kannst, und ein Playbook, das gerade entsteht. Welche Branchen wir angehen und mit welchen Kampagnen, verantworten unser Head of Sales und unser CRO. Dein Part ist das Gespräch, und was du dort hörst, fließt direkt in die nächste Runde ein. Aufgaben Telefon ist dein Hauptkanal. Cold Calling ist der Kern der Rolle, nicht ein Kanal unter mehreren. E-Mail und LinkedIn ergänzen die Ansprache Ziellisten aus den Verticals abarbeiten, die Head of Sales und CRO festlegen. Die Listen kommen aufgebaut aus Clay und Cognism. Du priorisierst innerhalb der Liste und bereitest jeden Account kurz vor, bevor du anrufst Kampagnen und Sequenzen in Lemlist setzen Head of Sales und CRO auf. Du führst sie aus und passt deinen Gesprächseinstieg im Call an dein Gegenüber an. Lemlist ist dein täglicher Arbeitsplatz, Clay und Cognism füttern ihn Erstgespräche buchen, sauber vorbereiten und mit belastbarem Kontext an die Account Executives übergeben Zurückspielen, was du im Markt hörst: welche Branche reagiert, welche Botschaft funktioniert, welche Einwände wiederkehren. Marketing und Sales-Leitung brauchen das HubSpot sauber und aktuell halten — nicht als Selbstzweck, sondern weil Pipeline-Bewertung und Forecast darauf beruhen. Enge Abstimmung mit Marketing und den AEs zu Kampagnen und Übergabekriterien Qualifikation Mindestens 1,5 Jahre Outbound-Erfahrung im B2B , idealerweise SaaS oder erklärungsbedürftige IT-Lösungen. Du musst nicht alles gesehen haben, aber du solltest den Job kennen und nicht bei null anfangen — ein spürbarer Teil dieser Zeit sollte am Telefon stattgefunden haben und nicht nur in Sequenzen. Das ist keine Einstiegsposition. Deutsch verhandlungssicher auf muttersprachnahem Niveau (C2), Englisch mindestens C1. Beides täglich. Der Maßstab ist das Telefonat: Du führst auf Englisch ein Kaltgespräch, reagierst auf Einwände und hältst den Small Talk davor und danach aus, ohne dass die Sprache zum Thema wird. Wir hören uns das im Prozess an. Du kannst nachvollziehbar erklären, warum deine Ansprache funktioniert hat — mit Zahlen und mit einer Begründung, nicht mit Bauchgefühl. Du kommst mit Geschäftsführerinnen und Inhabern zurecht. Im Mittelstand hast du häufig direkt die Person am Telefon, die entscheidet — und die dir drei Minuten gibt, bevor sie wieder in den Betrieb muss. Erst in größeren Häusern sprichst du mit Fachbereichsleitungen und gelegentlich mit der IT. Recherchefähigkeit: Du findest heraus, wer in einem Unternehmen ein Problem hat, bevor du zum Hörer greifst. Selbstorganisation: Du strukturierst deine Woche selbst und brauchst keine tägliche Ansage, um in die Aktivität zu kommen. Ein realistisches Verhältnis zu Ablehnung. Der größte Teil deiner Versuche führt zu nichts. Das ist normal und sollte dich weder überraschen noch aus der Ruhe bringen. Sicherer Umgang mit CRM und Sales-Engagement-Tools. Unser Stack ist HubSpot, Lemlist, Clay und Cognism — genau diese Tools musst du nicht kennen, vergleichbare schon. Du arbeitest selbstverständlich mit KI-Tools. Recherche verdichten, Textvarianten durchspielen, ein Unternehmen vor dem Call in fünf Minuten verstehen — das geht heute schneller, wenn man weiß wie. Wir erwarten keine Zertifikate, aber auch niemanden, der ChatGPT einmal ausprobiert und wieder weggelegt hat. Von Vorteil: Du hast schon aktiv nach Großbritannien akquiriert und kennst den Unterschied im Gesprächseinstieg. Ebenfalls hilfreich: Erfahrung mit Low-Code/No-Code-, ERP-, CRM- oder Datenbankthemen. Formale Abschlüsse sind uns weniger wichtig als belastbare Outbound-Praxis. Wenn du das kannst, interessiert uns dein Studienfach nicht. Benefits Was wir bieten 60.000 – 70.000 € Zieljahresgehalt (OTE) bei einem Split von 70 % Fixum und 30 % variabel. Der variable Anteil hängt an Kriterien, die du beeinflussen kannst, und ist erreichbar geplant. Den Plan legen wir vor Vertragsunterschrift offen. Strukturierter Einstieg: Produkt, ICP, Einwände und Gesprächsleitfäden in den ersten Wochen — plus regelmäßige 1:1s und Call-Reviews statt Zurufmanagement. Kurze Wege. Du berichtest an Tim Genkinger, unseren Head of Sales, und hast direkten Zugang zu den Menschen

10d78e301ef3.title: Senior RAMS Engineer
10d78e301ef3.description: We are looking for a RAMS Engineer to strengthen our safety and compliance team, with a particular emphasis on safety engineering for our vehicles, propulsion systems, ground infrastructure, and operations. RAMS covers Reliability, Availability, Maintainability, and Safety. This role will apply those principles across the full lifecycle of complex hardware and operational systems, helping ensure that hazards are identified early, risks are controlled, and safety requirements are supported by clear technical evidence. Although the role sits within safety and compliance rather than systems engineering, you will need a strong systems-engineering background and experience working with high-reliability, high-safety, or mission-critical systems. About us We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications. We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, generating significant revenue and applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket. We are working hard to build something truly spectacular. To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you. At our company, job titles and career progression are earned, not determined by years of experience alone. They reflect the responsibility you take on and the dedication you bring to each project. If you’re ready to rise to the challenge, we’d love to hear from you. Key responsibilities Establish and develop RAMS and safety-engineering processes across vehicles, propulsion systems, ground systems, facilities, and operations. Define, manage, and verify reliability, availability, maintainability, and safety requirements throughout the system lifecycle. Lead hazard identification, risk assessments, failure-mode analysis, fault-tree analysis, and other structured safety assessments. Develop and maintain safety cases, hazard logs, RAMS plans, safety assessments, compliance evidence, and technical justifications. Work with systems, propulsion, avionics, test, manufacturing, operations, and suppliers to identify hazards and implement effective risk controls. Support design reviews, test-readiness reviews, operational-readiness activities, incident investigations, change control, and corrective actions. What we are looking for Proven experience in RAMS, safety engineering, reliability engineering, or systems engineering for high-reliability, high-safety, or mission-critical systems. Experience analysing complex hardware and operational systems, including interfaces, failure modes, hazards, and system-level risks. Strong understanding of safety-engineering methods and the ability to turn analysis into practical design and operational controls. Experience producing clear technical documentation, safety arguments, risk assessments, compliance evidence, and engineering reports. Strong communication skills, with the confidence to challenge technical decisions and work effectively with specialist engineering and operational teams. A degree in systems engineering, safety engineering, aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, or a related discipline; equivalent practical experience may also be relevant. Desirable experience RAMS or safety engineering within aerospace, space, defence, rocketry, missile systems, nuclear, rail, energy, automotive, or another high-consequence industry. Experience with FMEA, FMECA, fault-tree analysis, hazard analysis, HAZOP, STPA, bow-tie analysis, or similar techniques. Safety cases, functional-safety assessments, reliability predictions, maintainability analysis, or probabilistic risk assessment. Propulsion systems, solid rocket motors, hazardous materials, explosives, test stands, launch operations, or high-energy systems. Experience supporting verification and validation, qualification, acceptance testing, configuration control, and engineering change processes. Familiarity with applicable aerospace, defence, functional-safety, quality, or hazardous-operations standards and regulatory frameworks. Fluent German would be a significant advantage in this position. Benefits and important information: We offer top-decile compensation packages, bonuses and meaningful equity, to attract exceptional aerospace talent. Every employee is awarded stock options in the company, you will directly benefit from your own hard work and success. Comprehensive relocation support including flights, shipping and visas. Lunch, dinner and drinks provided everyday Free access to shared company housing Please note, we are a fast paced, hyper-scaling startup. You will need to be comfortable working extended hours with high levels of autonomy, ownership, and flexibility, with contracts structured around a 48-hour working week. We are committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, has equal access to opportunity, and can thrive. We welcome different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences—and believe our differences make us stronger. Please submit applications in English Compensation: €80K – €95K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus • €80K – €95K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

3d4197b1d260.title: Accounting Expert: AI Model Evaluation
3d4197b1d260.description: About Huzzle Labs Huzzle Labs partners with frontier AI labs to evaluate and improve frontier models through deep human expertise. Contributors directly assess advanced AI systems in their specialist fields, receive competitive compensation, and help define the standards used to measure model performance. About the Role Huzzle Labs is seeking experienced accountants to write realistic accounting tasks that test how well frontier AI systems handle accounting work. You will create prompts that are difficult enough for a frontier model to fail, then write a scoring rubric for each task so reviewers can assess the output consistently. A rubric is a list of objective, checkable criteria that a reviewer marks pass or fail. Your judgement helps define the standards used to measure model performance. This is an expert judgement role focused on realistic task design, careful review of model output and precise, consistent documentation. Training is provided. Prior AI training or data-annotation experience is required. Responsibilities Write realistic accounting tasks: Create requests of the kind a client, controller or business owner would send, covering month-end close, bank and credit card reconciliations, AR/AP ageing, accruals and adjusting entries, sales tax, job costing and the clean-up of incomplete or inconsistent books. Build from real material: Review a deal room containing hundreds of files, select the relevant documents and use them to develop prompts and rubrics for tasks a frontier model struggles to complete correctly. Require usable deliverables: Each request should call for a working output, usually a spreadsheet, a journal entry schedule or a short memo. Test against a frontier model: Run each request and review the output with the care you would apply when signing off accounting work. Where the model succeeds, increase the difficulty until a genuine gap appears. Write scoring rubrics: Define objective criteria that another reviewer can apply without repeating your work, for example, “the reconciled ending balance equals $X” and “the $X deposit is recorded as a customer deposit liability, not revenue.” Apply guidelines consistently: Follow the task and rubric guidelines, flag ambiguous cases and help refine the criteria. Requirements At least 5 years in accounting, bookkeeping or finance operations. Prior AI training or data-annotation experience is required. Hands-on knowledge of month-end close, reconciliations, AR/AP, accruals and adjusting entries, sales tax and job costing. Excellent written English and precision with numbers. Careful and detail-oriented: accurate figures and objective, checkable criteria. Available 20 to 40 hours per week for an initial one-week trial, with potential extension. Example Assignment For a client deal room covering a small business with incomplete and inconsistent books, you would: Review the files and select the relevant documents, such as bank statements, ledgers, invoices and ageing reports. Write a prompt as the business owner or controller would, asking for a reconciliation and the adjusting entries needed to close the month. Run the prompt against a frontier AI model and check the spreadsheet or journal entry schedule line by line. If the model completes the task correctly, increase the difficulty, for example, by adding a customer deposit, a timing difference or a sales tax complication, until it fails. Write the rubric, such as “the reconciled ending balance equals $X” and “the $X deposit is recorded as a customer deposit liability, not revenue,” so another reviewer can grade any answer without repeating the work. Confidentiality An NDA must be signed before the engagement begins. Benefits Compensation: $60 - $90 USD / hour Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

3650ba4153cd.title: Research Scientist - Control & Machine Learning
3650ba4153cd.description: At Gigaton, we’re on a mission to cut gigatonnes of carbon emissions from the world’s biggest emitting industries (like cement, steel and glass), by building autonomous AI control and optimisation systems that learn and leverage the physics of manufacturing. Our products run heavy industrial plants more efficiently, more stably, and with lower emissions in real time - laying the foundation for the next industrial revolution. We are a team of scientists, engineers, builders, and operators who love hard problems, have high standards, and want to make change happen in the physical world. We care about deep tech, but we care even more about whether it delivers cost and carbon impact in a live plant, with real people, under real constraints. With Gigaton, you’ll solve really tough problems in places few people ever get close to, and build something that actually helps the planet. Are you up for the challenge? Research questions you could initially work on Learning dynamics from operational data. How can we identify useful models of a plant from noisy, partially observed data collected during closed-loop control? Optimising under uncertainty. How can Bayesian optimisation improve plant performance when experiments are expensive, samples are noisy, and operating constraints must be respected? Learning while controlling. How can we use dual control and active learning to choose actions that improve performance while gathering information about uncertain dynamics? Learning across plants. Which parts of a model or control strategy can transfer between plants, and how can we adapt them efficiently to a new site? These are meant as examples rather than an exhaustive list. We’re looking for someone who can bring depth to a relevant area, identify promising connections, and help us decide which problems to tackle next. Your main responsibilities As a Research Scientist, you’ll: Help shape our research and development agenda, turning challenges from live plants into well-defined research problems. Develop and implement methods for modelling, identification, optimisation and control of complex physical systems. Design rigorous experiments, establish strong baselines and understand when and why a method works. Work with process engineers to incorporate plant physics, operating knowledge and constraints into models and algorithms. Work with machine learning and deployment engineers to evaluate promising methods and bring them into production. Follow deployed performance, investigate failures, and use what you learn to guide further research. Communicate your findings clearly and contribute to the team’s scientific understanding. What a great fit looks like A PhD in control, machine learning, applied mathematics, engineering, physics or a related field, or equivalent research experience. A strong research background in one or more of control theory, data-driven control, system identification, Bayesian optimisation, probabilistic modelling, physics-informed machine learning, imitation learning or model-based reinforcement learning . Evidence that you can formulate a research question, develop a method and evaluate it carefully, through publications, open-source work or applied research. Strong Python skills and experience implementing machine learning models using tools such as Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, PyTorch. An interest in working closely with engineers and taking responsibility for how your methods perform in practice. Practical experience deploying machine learning and control algorithms. A strong interest in climate mitigation. You don’t need to know about cement. You do need to get excited about the physics, willing to learn from operators and process engineers, and keen to understand why a plant behaves the way it does. We don’t expect you to tick every box. If you bring depth in a relevant area and these problems excite you, we’d like to hear from you. In return for your hard work, we’ll give you 📈 Equity in the company: When we win, you win. You’ll get share options, so you’re part of our journey from the inside. 🕰️ Flexible working We trust you to know how and when you work best and to work that out with your team. 🌴 30 days of holiday (plus bank holidays). Rest is productive. Take the time you need to recharge 🪙 A generous pension scheme. We’re planning for the future in more ways than one. Our Operating Principles ↗️ Go Gig or Go Home : High Bar, All In. What we do matters to humanity, to our customers and to each other. We hold ourselves to an extraordinarily high bar and bring the urgency this mission requires. 🏭 Concrete Honesty : Be honest. As concrete forms the foundation of our world, genuine honesty and transparency are the bedrock of our culture. 🦾 Autonomous Ownership : High agency, high ownership. We build systems that take control and make things better. We do the same: see it, own it, drive it. 😄 Cement it with Kindness & Fun : Have fun, be kind. We're here to extend Earth's life, but ours is still limited. We want to enjoy the ride. To see these in full, go to Gigaton’s Operating Principles Notion page.
