About the Team

The Privacy Engineering team builds secure, reliable systems that help OpenAI meet its legal obligations while protecting user data. We partner closely with Legal and Engineering teams across OpenAI to support lawful data access requests and other critical legal workflows. Our work turns complex, high-stakes processes into auditable and dependable technical systems with clear human oversight and strong privacy and security controls.

About the Role

We’re looking for a full-stack Software Engineer to build the internal tools and data pipelines that power lawful data access request workflows and Legal Operations. You will work across product and data systems to make authorized retrieval and case handling accurate, efficient, and auditable. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys translating ambiguous operational requirements into durable systems, cares deeply about sensitive-data handling, and wants to improve both technical reliability and the day-to-day experience of the people operating these workflows.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, with two additional locations under consideration: London, UK, and Dublin, Ireland. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Design, build, and operate backend systems and workflow tooling for the full lifecycle of lawful data access requests, from intake and scoping through authorized retrieval, review, preparation, and audit.

 - Build reliable data pipelines and interfaces across products and data stores so authorized teams can locate and handle the right records accurately and reproducibly.

 - Implement least-privilege access, approval gates, provenance, audit trails, data minimization, and safe failure modes for sensitive workflows.

 - Partner with Legal and Legal Operations to translate legal and operational requirements into clear technical designs and intuitive operator experiences.

 - Identify responsible automation opportunities that reduce repetitive work while preserving human review, judgment, and accountability.

 - Own production systems through testing, observability, incident response, documentation, and continuous reliability improvements.

 - Help define the architecture and roadmap for reusable privacy and legal-infrastructure foundations as OpenAI’s products and obligations evolve.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have experience building or operating systems for lawful data access requests and understand the domain’s legal-process lifecycle, privacy and security constraints, auditability requirements, and operational sensitivities.

 - Strong backend engineering fundamentals and experience building production services or data-intensive systems.

 - Ability to reason carefully about correctness, authorization, security, and privacy when working with sensitive data.

 - A track record of turning ambiguous requirements into pragmatic plans and communicating technical tradeoffs clearly.

 - End-to-end ownership, including operating what you build, and comfort learning unfamiliar products and domains.

 - Care for operator experience and a drive to make complex workflows safer, clearer, and more efficient.

The Strategic Finance team at OpenAI plays a critical role in shaping the company’s long-term trajectory. We are developing scalable forecasting infrastructure to help us understand and anticipate business dynamics in an increasingly complex, usage-based world. Our models are foundational to planning, pricing, operational efficiency, and growth strategy - supporting key investment decisions and unlocking OpenAI’s full potential.

We’re looking for a senior Machine Learning Data Scientist to lead our forecasting initiatives. You’ll be one of the founding members of the Forecasting pillar within Strategic Finance Data Science, responsible for building and scaling robust, interpretable, and production-ready forecasting systems. Your models will power critical business decisions by predicting core metrics such as DAU/WAU, revenue, LTV, compute consumption, and profitability.

 

This is a highly cross-functional role, requiring technical excellence, strong product intuition, and business acumen. You’ll collaborate with product managers, researchers, engineers, and finance leaders to operationalize forecasting insights, influence company-wide strategy, and build foundational forecasting capabilities at OpenAI.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

1615e46c1a3b.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking an Electrical Engineer for a senior individual-contributor role leading printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) test infrastructure for advanced robotic systems. You will independently turn evolving requirements into working test stations, make technical tradeoffs, and own delivery from architecture and circuit design through validation, deployment, and reliable operation.

This role combines development-lab work with deployment at contract manufacturers. You will develop electrical test systems for board bring-up, programming, functional test, and characterization, partnering with mechanical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and reliability teams to carry validated stations from prototypes into repeat builds.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week. Travel to contract-manufacturer sites is part of the role, with timing based on build and deployment needs.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own PCBA test-station architecture, including device-under-test interfaces, programmable power, electronic loads, signal routing, instrumentation, and protection.

 - Translate board requirements and likely failure modes into test coverage, measurement methods, and pass/fail criteria. Partner with board designers on design for test, test-point access, programming interfaces, and diagnostics.

 - Design and bring up fixture interface boards, switching circuits, harnesses, and connectors. Release schematics, PCB layouts, wiring diagrams, bills of materials, and interface definitions.

 - Integrate oscilloscopes, meters, power supplies, loads, and data acquisition hardware; validate calibration, timing, accuracy, and repeatability across stations and board revisions.

 - Develop and debug programming and communications interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, and Ethernet as required by the board. Diagnose power, signal-integrity, grounding, and contact problems.

 - Design and validate current limiting, power sequencing, ESD protection, interlocks, and fault recovery appropriate to the hardware under test.

d4355d6fa95f.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an Electrical Engineer to develop the AI inference compute systems that power OpenAI’s humanoid robots. This role combines compute architecture, high-speed digital design, onboard power electronics, and compact HDI PCB development.

We’re looking for a self-driven engineer who takes ownership from concept through deployment. Above all, you should enjoy hands-on engineering: bringing up boards, characterizing interfaces, and tracking challenging failures to their root cause.



IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own compute hardware architecture and development, from component selection and schematic design through PCB layout, validation, and deployment.

 - Design and integrate high-speed interfaces—including PCIe, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, USB, and DisplayPort—balancing bandwidth, connectivity, power, and signal integrity.

 - Develop onboard DC-to-DC conversion and power distribution to meet efficiency, transient-response, sequencing, and power-integrity requirements.

 - Define HDI PCB stackups, dielectric materials, via structures, and routing strategies that balance electrical performance, manufacturability, reliability, and cost.

 - Lead bench bring-up and validation, including test planning, high-speed interface characterization, power measurements, and debugging through verified resolution.

 - Partner with thermal, mechanical, EMC, and software teams to integrate compute hardware into tightly constrained robotic systems.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 5+ years of experience developing compute hardware or similarly complex high-speed electronics, with demonstrated ownership of complete designs.

 - Bring strong hands-on measurement and debugging skills, including practical experience with oscilloscopes, probing techniques, and interface validation.

 - Understand high-speed digital interfaces deeply enough to make architectural tradeoffs and diagnose issues across hardware and software boundaries.

 - Have strong signal-integrity and power-integrity fundamentals, a solid foundation in power electronics, and practical experience designing complex HDI PCBs.

 - Can use a Linux shell, write simple shell scripts, connect over SSH, and perform basic Ethernet and network troubleshooting.

 - Take initiative, turn ambiguous requirements into concrete engineering plans, and follow through to deliver working systems.


ADDITIONAL, PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Experience designing around AI inference SoCs or accelerators, including their power, memory, and communication architectures.

 - Familiarity with how AI inference workloads map to silicon capabilities, including compute throughput (TOPS), DRAM bandwidth and capacity, and how workload requirements and DRAM technology choices affect achievable performance and performance per watt.

 - Experience bringing compute hardware into production and resolving fabrication, assembly, or test issues with manufacturing partners.

2181352e4747.description:
About the Team

The Product Policy research team studies how people use and experience AI, generating evidence to inform product, policy, and safety decisions. We partner with researchers, data scientists, engineers, and cross-functional teams to understand AI’s effects on people’s lives, including well-being, youth experiences, and social and emotional use.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Applied Scientist to help design, execute, and analyze large-scale longitudinal research on AI use and well-being. You’ll work closely with research leads to translate scientific questions into rigorous studies, combining survey responses with behavioral data to understand how people’s experiences with AI evolve over time.

This is a hands-on role spanning applied analysis, research methods, and study execution. You’ll build reproducible analytical workflows, assess data quality and representativeness, and help establish reliable infrastructure for ongoing panel research. Your work will support research involving teens and adults, including studies of AI companionship, and help turn findings into useful evidence for product, policy, and safety partners.

In this role, you will:

 - Partner with research leads to develop study designs, survey measures, and analysis plans for longitudinal research on AI use and well-being.

 - Conduct statistical analyses of survey and behavioral data, including evaluating selection and response bias, account-linkage patterns, and sample representativeness.

 - Prepare and validate analysis-ready datasets, implement analysis plans, and produce clear summaries and visualizations using reproducible workflows.

 - Develop quality checks across survey programming, fieldwork, data delivery, and repeated study waves to identify inconsistencies and improve research reliability.

 - Own day-to-day study execution, coordinating timelines, vendors, and cross-functional dependencies to deliver high-quality research on schedule.

 - Collaborate with data engineering and privacy partners on responsible account linkage, data flows, logging, and retention.

 - Support human-subjects research review, including Institutional Review Board (IRB) documentation, protocol amendments, and consent and assent processes.

 - Maintain clear documentation of methods, measures, assumptions, and protocol changes, and contribute analysis and methodological materials for research readouts, publications, and peer review.

 - Communicate findings, limitations, and practical recommendations to technical and nontechnical partners, and build reusable tools and processes that improve future studies.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have experience conducting applied quantitative research in social science, behavioral science, human-computer interaction, statistics, or a related field.

 - Bring strong foundations in survey research and statistical analysis, with experience working on panel studies, longitudinal datasets, or human-subjects research.

 - Are comfortable using SQL and Python or R to prepare data, implement analyses, validate results, and create visualizations.

 - Understand how recruitment, missing data, participant attrition, and measurement choices can affect the interpretation and generalizability of findings.

 - Can move between analytical work and practical execution, managing multiple timelines and collaborators while maintaining scientific rigor.

 - Communicate clearly, lead with the key takeaway, and connect methodological choices and findings to the decisions they inform.

 - Exercise sound judgment when working with sensitive data and research involving minors.

 - Enjoy building structure in ambiguous environments and collaborating across disciplines.

Nice to Have

 - Experience combining survey responses with behavioral or product data.

 - Familiarity with preregistration, measure validation, reproducible research, and academic publication or peer-review processes.

 - Experience working with research vendors, survey platforms, or IRB and ethics-review partners.

 - Research experience related to AI-human interaction, digital well-being, youth development, or social and emotional uses of technology.

f81a7cdc311a.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.

The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval. We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Researcher to work on semi-structured knowledge graphs within Search. You’ll research and develop methods for mining structured information from heterogeneous, unstructured and semi-structured web content, making that information more accessible and useful to AI models.

The core questions are: What structure helps models find and use information? How can we extract it reliably at web scale? And how do we measure whether it improves the model’s ability to reason and answer questions? How do we design the system to be optimizable end-to-end?

You’ll work across research, data, and systems, exploring how advances in AI and compute can improve the way knowledge is extracted, organized, and retrieved. This work will support retrieval across OpenAI products and internal research efforts, with opportunities for scientific publication.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Develop methods to extract and connect structured information across diverse web sources, including entities, attributes, and relationships.

 - Build scalable approaches for transforming noisy, inconsistent content into useful knowledge representations.

 - Explore how models and compute can improve extraction quality and reduce the manual work involved in building knowledge systems.

 - Design evaluations that measure both the quality of extracted knowledge and its usefulness for retrieval and model reasoning.

 - Partner with researchers and engineers to integrate structured knowledge into Search and use model performance to guide improvements.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE

 - Deep experience in knowledge extraction, knowledge graphs, entity resolution, or related work that derives structure from large, heterogeneous datasets.

 - Strong machine learning and research skills, with experience developing and evaluating methods for real-world data.

 - A track record of building or scaling data and ML systems, particularly for web-scale extraction, indexing, or retrieval.

 - Experience independently driving open-ended technical problems from an initial idea through experimentation and implementation.

 - A first-principles approach to using AI and compute, with a willingness to rethink established methods as model capabilities improve.

4789e248f3ae.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.

The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval. We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information. In close partnership with researchers, we bring modeling advances into production and improve how AI systems discover, retrieve, and use knowledge.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Researcher to lead Search Integrity: the systems that distinguish useful web content from spam, manipulation, and other adversarial or low-quality material.

The challenge extends beyond evaluating individual pages. A page may appear credible in isolation, while its links, metadata, or relationships with other sites reveal coordinated manipulation. As AI makes convincing content easier to produce at scale, detection systems must adapt to increasingly sophisticated adversaries.

You’ll define the technical approach, build classifiers and evaluations, and shape how integrity signals influence what Search indexes and retrieves. Working closely with Search and broader Safety and Integrity teams, you’ll use frontier models to advance detection methods and bring them into production.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Define the technical direction for Search Integrity, identifying gaps and determining which problems and interventions to prioritize.

 - Develop AI and ML systems to detect spam, scams, phishing, malicious domains, prompt injections, and other adversarial or low-quality web content.

 - Discover useful signals across page content, links, domains, metadata, and relationships between websites, including patterns that reveal coordinated manipulation.

 - Build evaluations that measure detection quality and how integrity interventions affect the information Search surfaces.

 - Translate detection signals into indexing, ranking, and filtering decisions, improving what models can retrieve and rely on.

 - Serve as the technical owner for integrity within Search, partnering with researchers, engineers, and broader Safety and Integrity teams to build and deploy these systems.




YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE

 - Deep experience in web spam, search quality, adversarial content detection, or related integrity problems at scale.

 - Strong applied ML and research skills, with experience developing classifiers, detection methods, and evaluations for real-world systems.

 - An understanding of how adversaries manipulate content and links, coordinate across sites, and adapt to detection systems.

 - A track record of independently defining ambiguous technical problems and driving solutions from experimentation through production.

 - Experience working across research, engineering, and integrity teams while remaining hands-on with technical work.

 - A first-principles approach to using frontier models and compute, and a strong interest in keeping detection systems effective as adversaries evolve.

cb01768faf27.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!




ABOUT THE ROLE.

We’re building the next generation of agentic AI infrastructure at Cohere. This team sits at the intersection of ML systems, distributed infrastructure, and developer experience, creating the platform that powers autonomous AI agents at scale.

You’ll work on hard, forward-looking problems with few established patterns, including secure code execution, agent state management, model routing, identity and authentication, and resource management for long-running agent workflows.

This role is a strong fit for someone who combines systems depth with ML intuition. You should be comfortable building reliable infrastructure, thinking through distributed systems tradeoffs, and understanding how emerging agentic capabilities shape platform design.




WHAT YOU’LL WORK ON.

 - Secure execution environments for agent-generated code

 - Identity, authentication, and trust boundaries for agents

 - Model routing and orchestration across different model types and environments

 - Rate limiting, quotas, and resource management for agent workflows

 - State management, memory, and filesystem abstractions for agents.
   
   


IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL:

 - Turn emerging ML research ideas into production-ready infrastructure

 - Build core platform capabilities for execution, storage, and state management

 - Prototype and evaluate new technologies, then help decide what should move into production

 - Partner with research teams to shape infrastructure based on what future agent systems will need
   
   


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE:

 - Experience building production ML infrastructure with strong systems fundamentals

 - Hands-on work with agentic systems, multi-agent workflows, or agent development frameworks

 - Familiarity with model routing and LLM provider frameworks across different model types and environments

 - Experience with scalable, fault-tolerant distributed systems and Kubernetes

 - A track record of moving quickly on prototypes and making good decisions about productionization.
   


BONUS

 - Experience across on-prem, private cloud, and public cloud environments

 - Familiarity with storage systems, embedded databases, or filesystem abstractions

 - Experience with code execution sandboxes such as gVisor, Firecracker, Kata, or WASM runtimes

 - Interest in emerging ML infrastructure, edge inference, or browser-native models

 - Open-source contributions to LLM or agent infrastructure projects

 - Experience with identity, workload auth, or capability-based security systems.
   




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.

All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. 02dd78e5b99f.description:
WHO WE ARE

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.



Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

Truly unique opportunity to shape and scale self-optimizing paid marketing systems for Growth. This role exists to turn our performance marketing experimentation program from a prototype into the operating system. The opportunity calls for deep paid-growth expertise and a strong grasp of how channel mechanics, audiences, creative, measurement, experimentation, and automation fit together. You’ll set the strategy and operating model, and guide the agentic infrastructure that brings it to life. You’ll partner with BizOps, Strat Fin, Growth, Ecosystems, and Marketing across Meta, LinkedIn, Google, and ChatGPT, interpreting always-on geo, cohort, creative, and spend signals in context.

This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. 




WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE:

 - By day 90:
   
   - Map how geo, audience, creative, spend, measurement, experimentation, and platform constraints interact; establish an operating model that turns those signals into hypotheses, tests, and clear kill/scale decisions, with agents supporting execution.
   
   - Build a deep understanding of onboarding and activation, and how paid acquisition connects to downstream user quality; partner with Growth PM and Ecosystems PM on meaningful improvements.
   
   - Establish how AI and agents can strengthen the end-to-end decision system—from analysis and hypothesis generation to creative and audience development, experiment QA, and reusable workflows—improving decision quality, not only execution speed.

 - By the end of year one:
   
   - Graduate the program from managing the experimental budget to managing the majority of paid spend, while maintaining efficiency and Notion’s quality bar for ad creative.
   
   - Establish stronger measurement and a clear, connected view of which experiments move which metrics, why they work, and how results vary by user cohort; use that understanding to shape more personalized experiences.
   
   - Turn the system into a repeatable model for Demand Generation, raising the standard for experimentation, measurement, and agentic marketing infrastructure across the organization.




SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: 

 - Strong systems fluency across APIs, automation pipelines, and agentic systems. You can see how platform integrations, data, measurement, workflows, and constraints fit together; shape sound architecture and tradeoffs; and partner credibly with technical teams to make the system reliable.

 - Deep paid-growth subject matter expertise across platforms such as Meta, LinkedIn, and Google. You understand how channel mechanics, budgets, audiences, creative, and performance interact, and can connect those dynamics to real marketing outcomes.

 - Expert measurement and performance-analysis judgment: you can interpret geo, cohort, creative, and spend signals in context, identify meaningful patterns, understand what is driving them, and make clear kill/scale decisions.

 - Strong product and systems judgment across technical and marketing domains, with the ability to connect the parts into a coherent strategy and translate an ambiguous frontier into a system with a high quality bar.

 - High-agency cross-functional ownership: you can work across BizOps, Strat Fin, Growth, Ecosystems, and Marketing to align decisions and deliver the full loop from strategy through operating model and infrastructure to outcomes.




Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. WHO WE ARE

Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.



Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

Run growth experiments for Notion’s Startups and SMB programs. You’ll turn promising ideas into measurable customer and revenue growth, moving from a signal in the data to a live experiment and a clear readout. Unlike a narrowly scoped growth role, you’ll work across acquisition, product experiences, AI-enabled systems, and operations—partnering with Ecosystem Growth, Storytelling, Product, and Engineering. On a typical week, you might query behavior data, prototype an in-product flow, launch a campaign workflow, and decide whether the signal is strong enough to scale.

 

This role is based in New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. 




WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE:

 - Establish Startups and SMBs as a proving ground for growth ideas that can expand Notion’s acquisition, activation, and revenue.

 - By your 90th day, map the relevant funnel, data sources, and existing growth bets with partners, then ship and evaluate your first experiment from hypothesis to customer-facing launch.

 - By your 90th day, use AI as a practical collaborator by building an AI-assisted workflow for audience research, campaign iteration, quality checks, or analysis—with clear human judgment and data guardrails.

 - By the end of your first year, build and iterate a portfolio of growth programs, using SQL and customer research to identify overlooked opportunities and decide where to invest next.

 - By the end of your first year, turn the strongest experiments into reusable programs, playbooks, and measurement systems that other teams can run—and raise the bar for how Notion evaluates growth opportunities.




SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: 

 - A track record of shipping growth or operations projects, with a clear account of what you personally built and what changed as a result. This matters because the role owns the path from idea to measurable outcome.

 - Strong SQL and analytical judgment: you can work through messy data, test assumptions, and distinguish a promising signal from a misleading result.

 - Hands-on experience building campaigns or automated workflows in tools such as Customer.io http://Customer.io, Salesforce, or comparable platforms.

 - The ability to turn an ambiguous goal into a practical plan, unblock yourself where possible, and communicate clearly when you need help from another team.

 - Curiosity and learning agility, including a willingness to use AI as a real collaborator and to build better workflows as you learn what works.

dfc89bcf9781.title: Staff Product Designer - Platform Design
dfc89bcf9781.description:
The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.
Spotify runs on the tools we've built for ourselves. They help hundreds of teams ship every day to hundreds of millions of people around the world. Now, we're sharing them.
Spotify Technology brings our proven tools and services together for engineering organisations everywhere, from global enterprises to individual developers. As AI reshapes how software gets made, we're building on years of experience solving complex engineering challenges at scale.
Platform Design makes these powerful tools feel effortless. We shape the services, products and experiences used by Spotify's engineering teams and by developers around the world. We believe great design is a competitive advantage, and developer tools deserve the same care and craft as any consumer product.
As a Staff Product Designer, you'll combine product leadership with hands-on design and engineering. You'll shape the experience strategy for a key part of the Spotify Technology portfolio, establish a distinctive visual language, and turn internal tools into products customers love using. You'll work closely with product, engineering and marketing partners, reporting to the Spotify Technology Design Director.

What You'll Do
Lead complex design challenges from early exploration through to production, creating intuitive flows, interfaces, interactions and motion that make powerful developer tools easier to use. Shape the visual language of Spotify Technology, bringing consistency, personality and craft across product experiences and brand touchpoints. Transform tools built for Spotify's engineering teams into compelling commercial products that meet the needs of developers and enterprise customers. Bring design to life in code, building and shipping high-quality front-end experiences with close attention to performance, accessibility and detail. Set experience strategy across your product area, partnering with product and engineering leaders to influence priorities, guide decisions and shape the roadmap. Use prototypes, storytelling and experimentation to make complex ideas tangible, build alignment and help teams navigate trade-offs. Explore how generative AI and agentic tools can improve design and development workflows, while creating thoughtful experiences for products used by people and AI agents. Raise the bar for design craft across the team, championing design systems, inclusive experiences and a culture of collaboration, feedback and continuous learning.
Who You Are
You have a strong background in product design, with experience shaping complex digital products and delivering high-quality visual and interaction design. You're comfortable working across strategy and execution, setting a clear product direction while staying close to the details of design and delivery. You can build and ship user interfaces using a modern front-end technology stack, and enjoy bringing your designs into production. You understand how to create cohesive visual experiences across product and brand, with a thoughtful approach to interaction, motion and design systems. You bring an understanding of developer tools, enterprise software or platform products, including the challenges of designing for technical audiences. You use generative AI and agentic tools in your work, applying sound judgement about where they add value and where human expertise matters most. You're comfortable navigating ambiguity, using research, data and customer insights to make informed decisions and solve complex problems. You communicate ideas clearly, build trust across disciplines and influence product decisions through compelling design work and storytelling. You care about helping others grow, welcome different perspectives and contribute to an inclusive, collaborative environment where great work can happen.
Where You'll Be
This role is based in London, UK or Stockholm, Sweden We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

About the Team

The Identity Infrastructure Engineering team builds the identity and access systems that OpenAI’s researchers, engineers, and internal teams rely on to protect critical systems and data.

We partner with Research, Applied Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, and Security to make secure access practical across cloud and internal environments.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on software engineer to design and build high-scale, high-throughput secure access proxies and the distributed systems behind them. These are tier-zero services: researchers, engineers, and agents depend on them to reach critical infrastructure safely and reliably.

You’ll work at the intersection of networking, distributed systems, and infrastructure security, building the serving paths and control-plane integrations that connect identities to resources. Teleport is a core part of the current platform; the role also includes credential brokers, policy enforcement, and developer-facing integrations.

You’ll own the services you build from design and implementation through production. That means understanding human, agent, and workload traffic, improving throughput and tail latency, making authorization decisions auditable, and designing for safe multi-region rollout and recovery. We’re looking for someone who can turn a demanding security requirement into software that works well at scale and is straightforward for other engineers to use.

In this role, you will:

 - Design and implement secure access proxies, gateways, and credential brokers that provide narrowly scoped, auditable access to infrastructure and internal services while reducing standing privileges..

 - Integrate identity and access policy across clients, proxies, and target systems so approved permissions take effect promptly and access expires or is revoked when required. Ensure correct behavior when policy is stale or sessions remain active.

 - Build observability that explains the end-to-end access path: latency, errors, saturation, authorization decisions, and identity attribution, without leaking credentials.

 - Engineer safe multi-region rollouts, canaries, rollback, failover, and recovery. Validate changes with realistic test environments, load tests, and failure testing.

 - Keep core access services reliable, performant, and maintainable. Own production support, maintenance, upgrades, and incident recovery; ship durable fixes that reduce recurring failures, alert noise, and manual work.

 - Make secure access easy to adopt through reusable APIs, client tooling, diagnostics, and self-service workflows. Lead migrations that preserve critical workflows, with tested rollback and recovery paths and clear ownership across Infrastructure, Security, and SRE.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

 - Have built and operated production backend, proxy, networking, or infrastructure services with demanding scale or availability requirements.

 - Have practical networking depth and can reason about HTTP, TCP, TLS, DNS, routing, and load balancing across real request paths.

 - Can explain how you handled performance bottlenecks, partial failures, multi-region deployment, or a difficult production change in a system you personally built.

 - Understand authentication, authorization, least privilege, trust boundaries, credential handling, and the consequences of an access-control failure.

 - Have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience with Go, Rust, Python, or similar languages.

 - Use tests, profiling, telemetry, and reproducible experiments to debug across system boundaries and verify correctness, performance, and recovery.

 - Make practical scope decisions, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and follow through from code to production. Teleport or comparable access-platform experience is helpful; strong engineering and production ownership matter more than knowing every tool.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


WHY THIS ROLE?

We’re building the foundational infrastructure that will define how the world thinks about and deploys AI, and we want the sharpest, most driven, and most curious people to help us do it. As the head of the Data Foundation pillar of our Analytics and Data Insights team, you’ll lead the team that makes Cohere’s data trustworthy, governed, and available: the warehouse every analytics surface runs on, the pipelines that keep it fresh, the access model that keeps it secure, and the agentic analytics layer that lets anyone at Cohere (and their agents) ask questions of governed data directly.

Your team owns the full data lifecycle. You’ll run ingestion into BigQuery from internal and external data sources, orchestrate it in Airflow and Cloud Run, model the data warehouse in dbt, and serve the results through Looker, export APIs, and customer-facing analytics surfaces. Everything is provisioned as code in Terraform, and governance is part of the design: VPC service controls, IAM patterns, and documented access paths that let people and agents move fast without putting data at risk.

This role is both highly visible and highly impactful, and you’ll inherit a solid structure on which to build the rest of the stack: a Terraform-provisioned warehouse framework, dbt modeling conventions, an alerting and incident-response practice, and documentation patterns to keep everything discoverable. The roadmap is set with big bets in flight: scaling that framework across the company, standing up an internal analytics agent with a real eval harness, and consolidating institutional knowledge into a self-correcting and self-maintaining system that keeps context centralized, current, and documented, rather than dispersed and in people’s heads.

Responsibilities

As the head of the Data Foundation pillar, you will:

 - Build and lead the team. Hire and grow a team of data and infrastructure engineers; set the technical bar; develop strong talent and raise team performance, building leadership capability beneath you.

 - Set the roadmap from company strategy. Own and sequence the Data Foundation roadmap: the warehouse buildout, the agentic analytics program, data governance, and the platform work that unblocks our other pillars. You’ll make the trade-offs and carry the cross-functional impact that comes with them.

 - Own the data platform end to end. Ingestion (managed connectors and an open-source connector framework), orchestration on Airflow and Cloud Run, warehouse modeling in BigQuery with dbt (raw, core, mart layers), and serving through Looker, export APIs, and semantic layers. All of it provisioned as code in Terraform.

 - Own data governance. Define how humans, service accounts, and agents get access to governed data: VPC service controls, IAM patterns, documented onboarding paths, audit logs, and sensitive requests (including legal holds) handled to deadline.

 - Operate for reliability. Run the alerting and anomaly-detection framework, own data freshness SLAs, lead incident response and postmortems, and turn every incident into a durable standard so the same class of failure doesn’t recur.

 - Lead the agentic analytics program. Wire the semantic layer into an internal analytics agent, build the eval harness that measures its accuracy, and make the eval-driven call on where AI earns its way into production. Apply the same discipline to automating data engineering work itself.

 - Set the standard for analytics across the company. The medallion framework, naming conventions, and testing patterns your team maintains become the way other teams ship analytics data. You’ll onboard new domains onto it and keep the docs accurate to how the systems actually work.

 - Partner across the org. Work with the North product and engineering teams on the analytics surfaces that ship in the product (including a customer-facing analytics export), with Business Insights on marts for the business, with Security on data governance, and with Legal on compliance-critical data requests.


QUALIFICATIONS

You may be a good fit, if you have:

 - 10+ years of experience across data engineering, data infrastructure, or analytics platform work, with a strong management track record leading data platform or infrastructure teams

 - Serious hands-on history in data engineering or infrastructure before management. You can still read a Terraform plan, a dbt DAG, or an Airflow scheduler log and ask the question that matters

 - Production experience with cloud data warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar), workflow orchestration (Airflow or similar), and infrastructure as code (Terraform or similar)

 - Depth in data modeling: you think in fact and dimension tables, raw/core/mart separation, and semantic layers, and you have opinions on where tests and contracts belong

 - A record of setting a team’s roadmap from company or function strategy and delivering outcomes that span teams, with the cross-functional partnerships to match

 - Operational excellence you can point to: alerting you trust, SLAs you meet, incidents you run to ground and write up so they teach

b4327bf10ab8.description:
Mission Brief 

You will be a senior technical contributor within Combustion Devices, responsible for high-fidelity combustion CFD and the physical understanding required to design, assess and mature liquid rocket engine combustion hardware. You will apply reactive-flow simulation, combustion fundamentals and test correlation to injectors, preburners, gas generators, ignition systems and main combustion chambers, ensuring that designs are performant, stable, thermally robust and ready for manufacture and hot-fire testing. 

Your Role in Our Space Mission: 

  • Own and execute CFD analyses of reacting flows in liquid rocket engine combustion devices, from model definition and meshing through solution, verification, validation and technical recommendation. 
  • Develop and apply premixed, partially premixed and non-premixed combustion models for rocket-relevant propellant systems and operating conditions. 
  • Perform steady and transient RANS/URANS and, where justified, scale-resolving simulations such as LES to investigate mixing, ignition, flame stabilisation, combustion efficiency and unsteady heat release. 
  • Model injector and chamber flows including atomisation, evaporation, multiphase effects, real-gas behaviour, conjugate heat transfer and wall heat flux where relevant to the design question. 
  • Assess combustion stability and operability, including flame dynamics, pressure oscillations, injector coupling, acoustic interaction, chugging and high-frequency instability risks. 
  • Build robust CFD workflows in Simcenter STAR-CCM+ and Ansys Fluent, including geometry preparation, meshing strategies, solver setup, automation, post-processing and model-quality documentation. 
  • Correlate simulations against component, cold-flow and hot-fire test data; quantify model uncertainty and clearly define the limits of predictive confidence. 
  • Translate CFD results into practical design decisions for injectors, chambers, preburners, gas generators, igniters, cooling concepts and combustion-device interfaces. 
  • Work closely with design, thermal, structures, materials, test, engine systems and manufacturing teams to converge combustion-device designs and resolve multidisciplinary issues. 
  • Plan analysis and validation activities, review work from colleagues and external partners, and contribute to technical reviews, development roadmaps and risk-retirement plans. 
  • Advance combustion modelling methods, engineering standards and reusable best practices across the Propulsion organisation. 

 

Qualification Checklist 

  • MSc or PhD in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, computational engineering or a comparable technical discipline. 
  • Typically 5–10 years of professional experience in rocket propulsion, with substantial hands-on responsibility for combustion CFD and combustion-device development. 
  • Deep knowledge of fundamental combustion physics, chemical kinetics, flame structure, turbulence–chemistry interaction, ignition and extinction phenomena.

b962992992bb.title: Senior Powertrain Test Engineer (All genders)
b962992992bb.description:
At Stark, we forge the future of European and national security through cutting-edge, AI-driven technology and unmatched engineering precision. As a premier defence technology company, our mission is clear: to equip NATO Allies and their partners  with next-generation autonomous defence platforms and advanced AI-driven software built to perform in the world’s most demanding environments.

We believe that true security stems from relentless innovation. By combining elite engineering talent with agile technology and an AI-native operational culture, Stark turns complex defence challenges into field-tested, multi-domain solutions.

WHY JOIN US

  • The software and systems you work on directly protect personnel and defend European and national sovereignty.
  • You will work alongside industry-leading minds on autonomous systems, advanced propulsion, and secure cyber platforms.
  • We foster a fast-paced, collaborative environment where bold ideas are supported by serious R&D backing.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Our team is responsible for designing, optimizing, and validating high-performance electric propulsion systems for cutting-edge autonomous defense platforms. We combine multi-physics modeling, simulation automation, and rigorous empirical test correlation to build state-of-the-art power delivery architecture. As a Powertrain Simulation Engineer, you will work closely with hardware test, firmware, and systems engineering teams to bring next-generation flight platforms from concept to reality.

YOUR MISSION

As a Powertrain Simulation Engineer, you will be the driving force behind predicting, optimizing, and validating the performance of our electric Powertrain Systems (propulsion, inverter, battery and cells). You will manage the development and execution of complex 1D multi-physics models to simulate aggressive flight profiles and powertrain behaviors. You will build simulation pipelines, automate data analysis, and conduct virtual testing to guide architectural decisions and validate system capabilities before physical hardware is built.

WHAT YOU WILL DO AT STARK

  • Design, build, and maintain high-fidelity 1D models of the complete electric powertrain (including batteries, inverters, electric motors, and thermal management systems) using industry-standard tools.
  • Execute standard and custom simulation profiles—including high-power continuous discharge (simulating hover/climb), dynamic pulse loading, and extreme temperature conditions—to evaluate system-level performance and efficiency.
  • Conduct trade studies and sensitivity analyses to optimize powertrain component sizing, gear ratios, voltage levels, and thermal cooling strategies to maximize range and payload.
  • Work closely with the hardware test engineering team (e.g., Dyno and Battery Lab) to correlate 1D simulation results with empirical test data, continuously improving model accuracy and reliability.
  • Provide high-fidelity plant models to the firmware and systems teams to support the development of control algorithms and Software/Hardware-in-the-Loop (SIL/HIL) testing.
  • Develop scripts to automate the execution of complex simulation matrices, post-processing of results, and generation of performance reports.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE MISSION

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience in a simulation, modeling, or systems engineering role, specifically focused on electric powertrains, thermal systems, or battery performance.
  • Extensive experience with 1D multi-physics simulation software (e.g., GT-SUITE, Siemens Amesim, MATLAB/Simulink/Simscape, or Dymola/Modelica).
  • Strong understanding of electric powertrain fundamentals, including thermodynamics, heat transfer, electrochemistry, and electric motor dynamics.
  • Proficiency in scripting languages (e.g., Python, MATLAB) for data analysis and simulation automation, alongside proven ability to interpret physical test data into mathematical models.

Role Summary

The Senior AI Engineer (Agents & Applications) will design, build, and operate production-grade agentic systems that coordinate, optimize, and automate decision-making across the  design-build-operate lifecycle of AI factories. The role is a core contributor to the AI & Applications team’s Model-to-Grid product, connecting models, inference endpoints, benchmark intelligence, validated workload recipes, job-scheduler decisions, infrastructure telemetry, AI-factory operations, and grid-related constraints into safe, explainable, and measurable workflows.

The role will build more than conversational co-pilots. It will create agentic applications that ingest and reason over time-series telemetry, logs, traces, events, scheduler state, benchmark results, configuration data, operational documentation, incident records, and multimodal sources where appropriate. These applications will help engineers, operators, and customers move from observation to diagnosis, recommendation, planning, simulation, controlled execution, verification, and continuous improvement.

The engineer will define and implement the underlying agent architecture and engineering framework: orchestration, state and memory management, retrieval, tool use, specialized sub-agents, evaluation, safety controls, human approvals, observability, and deployment. The role will use fit-for-purpose self-hosted and external model endpoints, with close integration to the team’s inference platform.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate agentic applications supporting AI-factory planning, commissioning, validation, workload onboarding, benchmark analysis, model and recipe optimisation, scheduling, operations, maintenance, incident response, and continuous improvement.
  • Define reference architectures for single-agent, multi-agent, workflow-based, eventdriven, and human-in-the-loop agentic systems.
  • Build orchestration workflows using appropriate agent frameworks and libraries, such as LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Microsoft AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, CrewAI, PydanticAI, Haystack, DSPy, or equivalent custom-built frameworks.
  • Select the appropriate architecture for each use case rather than applying multi-agent 
    patterns by default:
    • Deterministic workflow and state-machine architectures for repeatable, high-confidence operational processes.
    • Planner-executor architectures for decomposing complex investigation, planning, and remediation tasks.
    • Supervisor-worker or manager-worker architectures for coordinating specialist domain agents.
    • Router architectures for selecting the right model, tool, knowledge source, workflow, or specialist agent.
    • Reflection, critic, verifier, or judge patterns for quality assurance, validation, and safety checks.
    • Event-driven architectures for responding to telemetry anomalies, workload failures, scheduler events, benchmark regressions, and operational alerts.
    • Human-in-the-loop architectures for high-impact recommendations, privileged actions, or changes to production environments.

The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit www.alpha-sense.com. Come join us.

About the Role: 

The Core Cloud Platform team is responsible for AlphaSense's entire cloud infrastructure, including AWS account management, networking, data storages, and Kubernetes clusters. We build the underlying platform that supports hundreds of services and is used by over 400 globally distributed engineers.

We're scaling into a cell-based architecture, and the number of cells we run is growing fast, taking our Kubernetes footprint from dozens of clusters toward hundreds. That takes the platform in three directions at once: infrastructure configuration becomes a first-class layer with its own lifecycle, independent of application code; provisioning a new cell becomes a days-long automated operation rather than a multi-week effort; and cross-cell control points become standard, reusable, and consistent everywhere.

This is a Principal Engineer role with real breadth within the cloud platform. You'll set the architectural roadmap for our cloud, Kubernetes, and storage platform as it scales with AlphaSense's growth, and take dedicated ownership of the cloud-side configuration and Helm chart layer that every service depends on. Data storages are a critical part of this surface, and we're looking for genuine depth there.

It requires a deep cloud of both operational and software development skills, the ability to lead ambitious technical programmes, and the credibility to set direction with Engineering leaders and very senior engineers across dozens of teams.

We're looking for someone who genuinely embraces AI tooling in their day-to-day work, appreciates the productivity value it brings, and is motivated to make our infrastructure ever-more AI friendly.

What You’ll Do: 

  • Own the architectural roadmap for our cloud, Kubernetes, and storage platform
  • Own cloud-side configuration and the Helm chart layer for Cloud Core
  • Build the cell registry and automate provisioning to take new cell setup from weeks to days
  • Design the cross-cell gate mechanism as the reusable standard checkpoint across every cell
  • Own, operate and evolve our Cloud and Kubernetes platform, including our data storage layers
  • Make operations (upgrades, patching, lifecycle management) routine across hundreds of clusters
  • Continuously improve the security, reliability, cost efficiency and performance of our infrastructure
  • Champion standards and drive initiatives to promote uniformisation and eliminate duplication
  • Enable truly self-service and agentic workflow patterns that support a Build it - Own it model
  • Build tooling and AI powered integrations that reduce the cognitive load in cloud 
  • Architect, design and implement simple and maintainable solutions

Who You Are:

  • Extremely experienced in Kubernetes and its various components, containerisation and AWS cloud
  • Proven track record of running Kubernetes and Cloud based production SaaS systems at scale
  • Experience operating Kubernetes as a large fleet with hundreds of clusters
  • Strong knowledge of data storages across SQL, MongoDB, ClickHouse and Elasticsearch
  • Strong operational and troubleshooting skill with Kubernetes, databases and messaging systems
  • Deep understanding of networking and production level usage of service meshes and gateways
  • Experience separating infrastructure configuration from application code at scale
  • Experience with cell-based, multi-tenant or multi-region architectures 
  • Proficiency in Python and Golang
  • Evangelist of highly performant CI/CD practices that are supportive of agentic workflows
  • Ability and desire to design, lead, influence and deliver on ambitious technical roadmaps

Nice to have:

  • Experience with Vespa
  • Automated provisioning of new environments, regions or cells end-to-end
  • Management of large fleets of Kubernetes clusters with lifecycle management tools 
  • Production usage of Hashicorp Vault or similar secret management systems

a7e80a8431a0.description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. What is The Role

Elasticsearch powers search, observability, and AI retrieval (RAG) for the world's largest organizations. We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer to lead competitive benchmarking initiatives within the Elasticsearch Performance team. 

You will develop representative workloads, automate reproducible experiments, and investigate how Elasticsearch compares with alternative systems. Your work will identify performance strengths, gaps, and tradeoffs, guide engineering improvements, and help customers make informed technical decisions.

This is a hands-on engineering role focused on building benchmarks and investigating performance, with technical publishing as a shared responsibility alongside engineering and content partners.

A typical investigation might ask how Elasticsearch and an alternative system compare under concurrent ingestion and hybrid search, at comparable retrieval quality and cost, and which engineering changes would improve the outcome. This role offers the opportunity to connect deep performance analysis with product improvements and public technical work.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Own prioritized competitive benchmarking initiatives across search, vector and hybrid retrieval, and analytical and observability workloads.
  • Build and maintain automated benchmark harnesses, datasets, query sets, and load profiles that reflect real-world usage, including concurrent ingestion and querying.
  • Design fair comparisons with documented system versions, configurations, tuning decisions, resource budgets, and functional differences.
  • Evaluate latency distributions, throughput, resource consumption, and cost efficiency. For retrieval workloads, measure performance at comparable recall or relevance targets.
  • Adapt and extend workload-appropriate tools such as Elasticsearch Rally, ClickBench, and vector search benchmark frameworks.
  • Investigate performance differences using profiling, system metrics, and controlled experiments; collaborate with engineering teams to identify causes and validate improvements.
  • Evaluate relevant self-managed and managed cloud deployments, including serverless offerings, accounting for scaling behavior and service constraints.
  • Work with engineering and technical content partners to publish reproducible benchmark artifacts and clear technical reports that explain methodology, findings, limitations, and tradeoffs.
  • Partner with engineering and product management to prioritize benchmark coverage and translate findings into actionable product improvements.

What You Bring 

  • Solid software engineering skills, with experience building maintainable automation and analysis tools in Python or another relevant programming language.
  • Hands-on experience evaluating and diagnosing performance in distributed systems, databases, or search infrastructure.
  • Depth in at least one relevant area (search, vector retrieval, analytical databases, or observability systems) and the ability to learn unfamiliar systems.
  • Experience designing representative datasets and workloads, including query patterns, concurrency, and ingestion behavior.
  • Sound experimental judgment, including repeated measurements, variability analysis, warm-up and cache effects, and the distinction between meaningful changes and measurement noise.
  • Experience building reproducible test environments and documenting configurations, procedures, and results.
  • Clear technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to explain complex findings and their limitations.
  • Solid collaboration skills and the ability to turn performance evidence into applicable engineering recommendations.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with Elasticsearch, Lucene, Rally, ClickBench, or vector search benchmark frameworks.
  • Experience measuring retrieval quality alongside latency, throughput, and resource usage.
  • Familiarity with cloud performance and cost analysis, including autoscaling and serverless systems.
  • Public technical writing, open-source contributions, or published benchmark studies.

d9b9024917bf.description: About Us Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact. We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem . Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work. At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team. Visit www.perk.com to learn more. Why this role, why now 12,000+ companies trust Perk with their travel and spend, and we've brought both together in one intelligent platform. Every booking, expense and invoice adds to a wealth of data at your fingertips, and now is the moment to enable teams to use this data intelligently to power better decisions, precise reporting, and to create cost and time savings for our customers. Come lead the team that makes all of this possible. The Role Data is at the core of Perk's innovation and the backbone of how we will evolve our products using new technology. As our VP of Data, you'll step into one of the most influential leadership roles in Builders (Data, Product, Design, Engineering) with a direct hand in shaping Perk's strategy and success, and we scale our multi product platform. You'll join a strong, talented team with a clear mandate to shape how we create exceptional products at Perk, using our proprietary data. Across travel, spend, and events, Perk holds a wealth of data that touches every booking, expense, invoice and payment. Your opportunity is to reshape it so it powers smarter, more intelligent products that keep us on the cutting edge of what is possible. This is a role for a data leader who thrives in fast-paced environments, scales high-performing organisations through senior leaders, and has the technical credibility to go deep when it matters. You'll join a top-notch leadership team where we elevate each other, build shared strategies and win together. You'll help define how we grow and make decisions, with accountability for data across the whole company. Your team You’ll lead a talented, collaborative and innovative team who are excellent at what they do. Together they power the work the business relies on every day, and they’re ready to take data to its next stage of scale with you. Your missions Strategy and Roadmap . More than ever data informs everything we do and is core to the AI native products that we build. 5e3d1939cdd1.description:
Overview

The Cybersecurity Engineer is a hands-on technical role within the Cybersecurity team, responsible for the day-to-day operation, monitoring and continuous improvement of the security controls that protect Cambridge Consultants’ systems, data and client work. As a small team, everyone contributes across the full breadth of the estate rather than owning a single system in isolation.

Reporting to the Head of Cybersecurity, you’ll work across a wide range of security systems and tooling alongside the rest of the Cybersecurity team, while collaborating with colleagues across IT Services and other business stakeholders to keep the organisation secure. Strong teamwork and a willingness to build knowledge beyond your immediate specialism are essential, given the breadth of technologies and responsibilities covered by the team.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Monitor and operate the team’s core security tooling, investigating alerts and coordinating remediation activities.
  • Manage vulnerability assessment activities, including vulnerability scanning, remediation tracking and maintenance of the risk register.
  • Support the operation of email security controls, including investigation and triage of suspicious email activity.
  • Review software requests, approving low-risk solutions and conducting more detailed security assessments where required, working with stakeholders across the business to understand requirements and risks.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of security monitoring, processes and operational practices.
  • Support the administration and improvement of identity, access management and endpoint security controls, including Active Directory, Entra ID, Conditional Access and endpoint management technologies.
  • Help deliver cybersecurity awareness activities, provide practical security guidance, and work with colleagues across IT and the business to support secure ways of working.
  • Contribute to security improvement initiatives and projects across cloud security, identity, monitoring and data protection technologies, informed by emerging threats and technology risks

What you need to succeed:

  • Experience investigating and triaging alerts from AV/EDR tooling (e.g. Sophos, Defender), including analysing Windows event logs, suspicious activity, email-related threats and Microsoft 365 security alerts.
  • Ability to assess and articulate security risk, including the relationship between threats, vulnerabilities and risk, with working knowledge of vulnerability management concepts such as CVEs, CVSS scoring and remediation prioritisation.
  • Experience supporting security incidents, with an understanding of the incident response lifecycle, evidence handling and reporting requirements.
  • Basic grounding in identity and access management (Active Directory, Entra ID, Conditional Access, SSO), Microsoft 365 security capabilities, and core networking concepts (protocols, ports, DNS, firewalls/VPN).
  • A team player with a strong willingness to learn, share knowledge and support colleagues across a small team covering a broad range of systems. This role requires breadth across many areas rather than deep specialism in a single technology.
  • Excellent communication skills at both technical and non-technical levels, with strong attention to detail, critical thinking and problem-solving.

What we offer:

  • 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays (with the option to buy 10 more a year)
  • Company bonus (profit share)
  • Flexible working patterns and hybrid working
  • Medical insurance and group income protection
  • Employee assistance programme and mental health support group
  • Enhanced maternity/paternity leave
  • Sabbatical leave
  • Travel insurance (business and leisure)
  • Generous company pension plan
  • Personalised career development and training plans
  • Free breakfast and two-course lunch in the office every day
  • Free onsite parking and we are close to public transport links
  • A variety of events organised by our social committee, ranging from summer and Christmas parties to board game nights and socials at our own rooftop bar!

Why Cambridge Consultants?

At Cambridge Consultants, you'll contribute to radical, new-to-the-world innovation that transforms business, society and the planet. Joining our multidisciplinary teams means helping to turn bold ideas into reality, harnessing the power of deep tech to create products, services and experiences that have never existed before. Whether you're advancing technologies, shaping strategy, supporting operations or driving commercial growth, it's an opportunity to make a real impact and help create the future.
